title: Yazidi women’s organizations call for international search for missing persons
content:
Twelve years after the genocide committed by the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS) against the Yazidis in Shengal, the fate of around 3,000 people remains unknown. The Free Yazidi Women’s Movement (TAJÊ) and the Umbrella Organization of Yazidi Women’s Councils (SMJÊ) have issued a joint appeal to 54 state and international institutions and political officials, calling for the establishment of an international search and rescue commission to locate abducted women and children in particular and secure their release.




The letter is titled “We demand freedom and justice for those abducted during the genocide of August 3, 2014.” The organizations recall that around 6,000 Yazidis were abducted during the ISIS attack on Shengal, and numerous families are still waiting for news of their loved ones although twelve years have passed since. “Every family whose loved ones are missing has the right to know the truth. Every person who remains in captivity has the right to freedom. And every victim of the genocide has the right to justice,” the letter reads.




Uncertain fate following the dismantling of al-Hol camp




The women’s organizations expressed particular concern about the situation in Syria. They said numerous abducted Yazidis were held in Idlib and other regions in the past, and the ongoing political and military instability is making it difficult to search for them. Another concern was the dismantling of al-Hol camp during the Syrian offensive against the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria at the beginning of this year. According to TAJÊ and SMJÊ, Yazidi women who had been unable to reveal their identities for fear of threats and reprisals were also among those held there.




Since the dismantling of the camp, TAJÊ and SMJÊ said, it has remained unknown where these women were taken and under what conditions they are currently living. The fate of other abducted Yazidis in Iraq and Turkey must also be clarified, they said and, in this context, referred to their campaign “For Justice and Freedom – Become a Voice for Those Abducted During the Genocide.” The campaign aims to prevent the crimes committed against the Yazidis and the suffering of their families from being forgotten as time passes.




Four demands to the international community




The letter focuses on four specific demands. First, TAJÊ and SMJÊ call for the establishment of a specialized international team involving the relevant states, international organizations, and other responsible bodies. The team would systematically search for those abducted, determine their whereabouts, and organize their release. Second, the women’s organizations demand that ISIS perpetrators be brought to trial not only for terrorist offenses but explicitly for genocide and crimes against humanity. They demand that the crimes committed against the Yazidis be prosecuted in accordance with international law.




As a third measure, they propose an international commission to investigate cases of missing persons. Scientific investigations, identity registries, and DNA analyses would be used to identify and locate abducted and missing persons and reunite them with their families. Finally, the organizations demand that states that have officially recognized the genocide against the Yazidis take practical steps to give effect to that recognition.




These include searching for missing persons, rescuing those abducted, protecting the rights of survivors, and prosecuting those responsible. “Recognition of the genocide is not merely a political and moral stance. It also entails far-reaching obligations,” TAJÊ and SMJÊ emphasized.




Letter sent to parliaments, governments, and UN institutions




The appeal was sent to a total of 54 government bodies, international organizations, and political officials. The recipients include the German Bundestag, the Federal Foreign Office, and the German Institute for Human Rights, as well as parliaments, ministries, and human rights institutions in Switzerland, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, Austria, Sweden, Luxembourg, Portugal, and Armenia.




Institutions in Australia, Canada, Ireland, and the United States, as well as the European Commission, the European Parliament, and several United Nations human rights bodies, were also contacted. Among the officials personally addressed was European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.




TAJÊ and SMJÊ emphasized that securing the release of those abducted was not solely the responsibility of the Yazidi community. Rather, they said, it was a humanitarian, moral, and legal responsibility of the international community. “We hope that these rights will not remain mere words but will also be realized in practice,” the joint letter concluded.

title: YRK reports Iranian drone and artillery attacks on Serdeşt region
content:
Iranian regime forces attacked areas in Serdeşt district in Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilat) with artillery and drones on Wednesday. According to the Press and Communication Center of the Eastern Kurdistan Defense Units (YRK), the attacks were concentrated particularly on the Mirava region.




According to the YRK, the shelling on November 18 lasted from 11 am to noon and was part of the Islamic Republic’s ongoing artillery and drone attacks on the region. The attacks reportedly caused damage to the natural environment and landscape. They also significantly disrupted the daily lives of local residents.




YRK underlined that the repeated attacks were fueling insecurity and concern among residents and making their living conditions and daily activities more difficult. The YRK reported that their forces had suffered no casualties or damage in the attacks.




Most recently, the Iranian regime carried out massive attacks on Serdeşt last week. In the ensuing clashes between the Revolutionary Guards and YRK units, guerrilla fighter Dersim Behar lost his life.




The YRK reported on Tuesday, November 17, that their units carried out two actions in the cities of Bane and Serdeşt regions.

title: Four lawyers remanded in custody in Izmir
content:
The police and prosecutorial procedures concerning the six lawyers, who were detained following raids on their homes on the morning of 17 November in Izmir, have been completed.




The six lawyers, including members of the Izmir Branch of the Progressive Lawyers Association (ÇHD), were transferred to the İzmir Bayraklı Courthouse. Following their statements to the prosecutor, they were brought before the Criminal Judgeship of Peace on duty, with prosecutors requesting their arrest.




Following their hearings, the court ordered the arrest of ÇHD Izmir Branch Secretary and lawyer Veysi Çetin, ÇHD members and lawyers Yemen Cankan and Erdoğan Akdoğdu, and lawyer Bahattin Özdemir.




Meanwhile, ÇHD member and lawyer Emrah Kanbay and lawyer Göksel Akbaba, who appeared before the court as part of the same investigation, were released subject to judicial control measures.

title: DEM Party to visit Abdullah Öcalan
content:
The Imrali delegation of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) will travel to the Turkish prison island of Imrali again in the coming days to meet with Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan. The delegation consists of members of parliament Pervin Buldan and Mithat Sancar, as well as lawyer Faik Özgür Erol.




The delegation last visited Öcalan on September 13. More than two months have passed since that meeting. An exact date for the upcoming visit has not yet been announced.




The announcement comes just days after new information emerged about Öcalan’s detention and working conditions. DEM Party Co-Chair Tuncer Bakırhan stated during his party’s parliamentary group meeting on November 17 that Öcalan had been moved to a residential area specially built for him on Imrali. Accordingly, his working conditions have also changed following the relocation. In addition, his secretarial support has been increased to enable him to work more quickly and effectively, Bakırhan stated.




The changes are linked to the ongoing peace and democratization process. In his speech, Bakırhan emphasized that, following the cessation of armed hostilities and the initiation of dialogue, the focus must now be on establishing the legal and political foundations and opening up space for democratic politics.

title: Hatimoğulları calls for strengthening local democracy in Adana
content:
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Co-Chair Tülay Hatimoğulları has accused the Turkish government of neglecting Adana’s economic development and weakening local self-government. At a meeting with neighborhood and village heads (muhtars) as part of the campaign “Budget for Bread, Peace and Justice,” she criticized the shifting of state investment incentives and agricultural policies that are accelerating the decline in agricultural production.




Hatimoğulları explained that muhtars were often the first point of contact for people affected by poverty, unemployment, and social exclusion. She remarked that women, unemployed young people, people with disabilities, and those without adequate access to social benefits, in particular, turned to them with their problems.




“Adana has lost its industrial base”




Hatimoğulları recalled that Adana had once been a major industrial and agricultural center that attracted workers from across Turkey. “The fertile lands of Çukurova provided a livelihood for many people. Industry was much stronger. But because investment incentives were shifted to other cities, Adana has lost its industrial base. Agricultural policies have also deprived the city of its agriculture. The plains of Çukurova, Harran, and Konya have the potential to meet the country’s food needs. Instead of utilizing this potential, however, the government is pursuing policies that undermine agricultural production,” Hatimoğulları said.




Elected mayors must be reinstated




Addressing government interventions in Adana’s municipal administrations, Hatimoğulları called for the reinstatement of elected mayors. She stressed that the arrests and removals from office not only disrupted the work of municipalities but also made it more difficult for muhtars to convey concerns from their neighborhoods to the relevant authorities.




The DEM Party Co-Chair continued: “The people of Adana elected Zeydan Karalar, but he is no longer at the head of the city administration. Although he was released from detention, he has not been reinstated. The elected mayor of Ceyhan, Kadir Aydar, was also released but has not been reinstated. Seyhan Mayor Oya Tekin is in prison. Following the operation against the Çukurova municipal administration, Emrah Kozay and other officials remain in detention. Can we still speak of local self-government and democracy under these circumstances?”




Hatimoğulları demanded that the affected mayors and municipal officials be allowed to stand trial without being held in detention and be reinstated in their positions. She also called for expanding the powers of municipalities and muhtars. “In the face of growing social hardship, they are often barely able to respond to the population’s requests for assistance. Real democracy does not emerge when everything is governed from Ankara. Real democracy emerges through the strengthening of local self-government.”




“Peace must not become an election campaign tool”




Regarding the peace and democratization process, Hatimoğulları described the absence of further news of deaths among Kurdish and Turkish young people as the most important achievement of the past two years. “This is enormous progress for us. We all know how much suffering and devastation each death caused among those affected. The fact that we no longer have to experience this is a major gain.” At the same time, she criticized the antidemocratic measures, police operations, arrests, and detentions for placing a strain on the process. She said the issue was the democratic and peaceful resolution of a century-old question which must not be subordinated to the interests of individual parties.




“Whoever tries to sacrifice this process for their narrow party-political interests, whoever fails to approach it sincerely and seeks to turn it into an election campaign tool, will be mistaken. No matter who they are. Because we regard this process as a genuine peace process. We want it to succeed, to ensure there is no turning back, and to prevent us from ending up where we started.” Hatimoğulları emphasized that the DEM Party had never viewed the process as an opportunity to gain partisan political advantages. She said this position applied equally to the governing parties and the opposition.




“We want the deaths to stop permanently. That is why we support this process. No party should reduce it to its own interests. We say this to both the governing parties and the opposition,” she stated.




Hatimoğulları called for broad public support: “Whether nationalist, social democratic, left-wing, or right-wing, we must come together as a society, as 86 million citizens, and focus collectively on peace so that we can establish it in this country.”




“Our doors are open to all citizens”




In closing, the DEM Party Co-Chair emphasized that her party was open to addressing the concerns of all social groups, regardless of ethnic origin, faith, or political affiliation. She called on the muhtars, who described the problems facing their neighborhoods and communities following her speech, to also bring any restrictions on their own rights to the party’s attention. “Our doors are open to all citizens – Turks, Kurds, Laz, Arabs, Circassians, Alevis, Sunnis, and Christians – and, of course, to you as muhtars. Tell us openly what problems you face and which issues should be raised in Ankara. Let us work together to do whatever is within our power.”

title: HPG releases names of seven fallen guerrillas from Merîwan
content:
The Press Center of the People’s Defense Forces (HPG) has released the identities of seven guerrilla fighters from the Eastern Kurdish city of Merîwan who lost their lives in various areas of Southern Kurdistan (Northern Iraq) between 2011 and 2024. In a statement, the HPG paid tribute to their commitment to the Kurdish freedom struggle and extended their condolences to the families of the martyrs.




The HPG statement said:




“We remember our comrades Rênas Botan, Kawa Hewraman, Sîrwan Qendîl, Hewrê Kemanger, Sîrwan Zirêbar, Serxwebûn Hewraman, and Serkeft Hewramî, who fought as steadfast militants committed to the Apoist principle of self-sacrifice, with respect, love, and gratitude.




Our comrades Rênas Botan, Kawa Hewraman, Sîrwan Qendîl, Hewrê Kemanger, Sîrwan Zirêbar, Serxwebûn Hewraman, and Serkeft Hewramî took up the struggle for freedom against the centuries-long oppression of our people and joined the struggle without hesitation, guided by the Apoist principle of self-sacrifice. They rejected colonial borders and the order that denies the existence of our people, and assumed a leading role in the struggle in the mountains of Kurdistan.




Despite the advanced military technology of our time, they relied solely on the strength of human will, consciousness, and conviction, setting an extraordinary example of courage and determination. They fought fearlessly to defend the existence of our people and, through their selfless commitment, embodied the unyielding will to resist colonialism.




Through their actions and unwavering commitment to the freedom struggle, they became an embodiment of the determination on which our resistance is founded. Our fallen comrades, who have secured a permanent place in the hearts of our people, have thus become guides toward a free future, an expression of our struggle, and a guarantee of its success. We extend our condolences to the esteemed families of our martyrs and to the entire patriotic Kurdish people. We pledge to remain faithful to their memory under all circumstances and to resolutely achieve the goals for which they fought.”




The HPG provided the following biographical information about the fallen guerrillas:

























Nom de Guerre: Rênas Botan


			First-Last Name: Mûctema Xoşnemek


			Birthplace: Merîwan


			Mother's-Father's Name: Mesûme – Ebdulrehman


			Date and Place of Martyrdom: 18 May 2020 / Metîna
















 

























Nom de Guerre: Kawa Hewraman


			First-Last Name: Mislim Edwayî




Birthplace: Merîwan


			Mother's-Father's Name: Fatime - Ebdulkerîm


			Date and Place of Martyrdom: 18 December 2011 / Qendîl
















 

























Nom de Guerre: Sîrwan Qendîl


			First-Last Name: Sena Keremî


			Birthplace: Merîwan


			Mother's-Father's Name: Çîmen - Eta


			Date and Place of Martyrdom: 20 December 2024 / Zap
















 

























Nom de Guerre: Hewrê Kemanger


			First-Last Name: Salim Muradî


			Birthplace: Merîwan


			Mother's-Father's Name: Walîde - Sabir


			Date and Place of Martyrdom: 9 June 2020 / Zap
















 

























Nom de Guerre: Sîrwan Zirêbar


			First-Last Name: Ednan Tazîk


			Birthplace: Merîwan


			Mother's-Father's Name: Şewket - Mehmûd


			Date and Place of Martyrdom: 9 June 2020 / Zap
















 

























Nom de Guerre: Serxwebûn Hewraman


			First-Last Name: Şahid Edwayî


			Birthplace: Merîwan


			Mother's-Father's Name: Rena - Muhsin


			Date and Place of Martyrdom: 5 September 2022 / Zap
















 

























Nom de Guerre: Serkeft Hewramî


			First-Last Name: Zana Semedî


			Birthplace: Merîwan


			Mother's-Father's Name: Şehla - Nasir


			Date and Place of Martyrdom: 19 October 2022 / Xakurkê
















 




Rênas Botan




Our comrade Rênas Botan was born in Merîwan into the long-established Pervez tribe. He grew up in a patriotic family with strong ties to Kurdish identity, language, and culture. This family and social environment shaped his national consciousness from an early age. He attended schools run by the Iranian regime for five years. Even during this period, he began examining the Iranian state’s policies toward our people and developed a critical attitude toward the assimilation-oriented education system. After leaving school, he worked as a shepherd to help support his family. Through this work, he learned at an early age to take responsibility and face life’s difficulties with determination.




In 2007, Comrade Rênas became more closely acquainted with the Kurdish freedom movement. Even before joining the guerrilla forces, he participated in the activities of its local structures. He took on responsibilities that required a high degree of discipline, a sense of responsibility, and confidentiality. He was particularly impressed by the militants’ attitudes, their close ties with the people, and the solidarity among comrades. During this period, he deepened his engagement with the philosophy of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] and the goals of the freedom movement. He also shared his convictions with those in his immediate circle. Together with his sister, he eventually decided to join the armed struggle for freedom. In 2009, both joined the guerrilla forces in the mountains of Kurdistan via Merîwan.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/45182c1b_20261116113346_2026-11-17-behdinan-renas-botan-muctema-xosnemek-18-05-2020-metina-sehit-sicil-1.mp4










Comrade Rênas received his initial ideological and military training in the Qendîl Mountains. The communal way of life of the guerrilla forces, the relationships among comrades, and life in the mountains left a deep impression on him. After completing his training, he initially took on various duties in Qendîl and put the knowledge he had acquired into practice. Following two years of practical work, he continued his training at the Şehîd Ibrahim Academy to deepen his ideological and military skills. There, he developed further both theoretically and practically and prepared to assume military leadership responsibilities.




When the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS) began its genocide against the Yazidi people in Shengal in 2014, Comrade Rênas insisted on taking part in their defense. He responded to Leader Apo’s call for mobilization and went to Shengal, where he participated in numerous operations against ISIS. He assumed important responsibilities in defending the Yazidi people and distinguished himself through his determination and commitment. After completing his mission in Shengal, Comrade Rênas returned to the Medya Defense Zones. He wanted to apply the military experience he had gained in the fight against ISIS to resisting attacks by the Turkish army.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/9332f912_20261116113316_2026-11-17-behdinan-renas-botan-muctema-xosnemek-18-05-2020-metina-sehit-nirxandin-1.mp4










He initially went to Heftanîn, where he participated in the defense against the Turkish occupation. He assumed responsibilities as a squad and platoon commander. He combined his military experience with close bonds with his comrades and active participation in communal life. Following his deployments in Qendîl, Shengal, and Heftanîn, he eventually continued his struggle in Metîna. Over many years, he had taken on responsibilities in different areas of Kurdistan and proved himself both in military confrontations and in the everyday life of the guerrilla forces.




On May 18, 2020, our comrade Rênas Botan fell in an enemy attack in Metîna. Through his determined attitude, his sincere bonds with his comrades, and his unwavering loyalty to the values of the freedom struggle, he left behind a significant legacy. We reaffirm our pledge to keep the memory of Rênas Botan and all our fallen comrades alive and to continue their struggle for a free Kurdistan. We extend our heartfelt condolences to his patriotic family from the Pervez tribe in Merîwan and to our entire people.




Kawa Hewraman




Our comrade Kawa Hewraman was born in the Hewraman region. He grew up in a patriotic family with strong ties to the Kurdish language, culture, and history of resistance. Hewraman is one of the regions of Kurdistan where the people have preserved their cultural identity, language, and social values despite decades of policies of assimilation and oppression. This environment shaped Comrade Kawa’s political consciousness from childhood.




He attended schools run by the Iranian regime for twelve years. He maintained a critical attitude toward the state ideology taught there and the policy of denying Kurdish identity. After completing his education, he worked in various technical occupations to help support his family. Through his work, he developed a strong sense of responsibility and close ties with working people.




The Iranian state’s policies of oppression and assimilation toward our people strengthened his desire to participate in the Kurdish freedom struggle. In 2009, Kawa Hewraman became more closely acquainted with the Kurdish freedom movement. Through his engagement with its political and ideological foundations, he became convinced that he had to make his own contribution to the struggle for the freedom and dignity of our people. In 2011, he decided to join the armed struggle for freedom and joined the guerrilla forces in the mountains of Kurdistan. He received his initial military and ideological training in the Qendîl Mountains.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/a752cae1_20261116113433_2026-11-17-behdinan-kawa-hewraman-mislim-edwayi-18-12-2011-qendil-sehit-sicil-1.mp4










From the outset, Comrade Kawa distinguished himself through his eagerness to learn, his curiosity, and his active participation in communal life. He engaged intensively with the paradigm of a democratic, ecological, and women’s liberation-oriented society developed by Leader Apo. In doing so, he sought not only to understand the theoretical foundations of the freedom movement but also to put them into practice in his own life. His sincere, modest, and supportive personality quickly earned him the respect and appreciation of his comrades. His willingness to assume responsibility, his commitment to communal life, and his determined dedication to the goals of the freedom movement characterized his time in the guerrilla forces.




On December 18, 2011, our comrade Kawa Hewraman fell in the Karox area of Qendîl. Although his time in the ranks of the guerrilla forces was brief, he left a lasting legacy through his determination, sincerity, and dedication to the freedom struggle. We will preserve the memory of Kawa Hewraman and carry forward his legacy in the struggle for a free Kurdistan and the freedom of Leader Apo. We extend our heartfelt condolences to his esteemed patriotic family, the people of Hewraman, and the entire patriotic people of Kurdistan.




Sîrwan Qendîl




Our comrade Sîrwan Qendîl grew up in Merîwan in a patriotic family belonging to the Xwekerem tribe. From childhood, she had strong ties to the Kurdish language, culture, and national values of our people. Her family environment and the tradition of resistance in her homeland shaped her political consciousness from an early age. She attended schools run by the Iranian regime for eleven years. Even during her school years, she recognized that the state education system was designed to alienate Kurdish children from their language, identity, and culture. She developed an increasingly critical attitude toward this policy of assimilation and deepened her connection to the social and cultural roots of her people.




At a young age, Sîrwan began engaging with the Kurdish freedom movement. Her cousin Abdurrahman Keremî, who had joined the guerrilla forces in 2014 under the name Sîrwan Merîwan, played a particularly significant role in this. The deaths of two guerrillas from her home village that same year also left a deep impression on her. These experiences strengthened her desire to actively participate in the freedom struggle.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/383baf84_20261116113559_2026-11-17-behdinan-sirwan-qendil-sena-keremi-20-12-2024-zap-sehit-sicil-1.mp4










She initially became involved in patriotic youth activities and engaged intensively with the philosophy of Leader Apo. His analyses of women’s liberation, in particular, influenced her political and personal development. Examining patriarchal power structures and the position of women in society became an essential part of her understanding of freedom.




When her cousin Sîrwan Merîwan fell in the Medya Defense Zones in 2016, it reinforced her decision to join the guerrilla forces. Due to various circumstances, she initially had to postpone this step. In 2018, she was finally able to put her decision into practice and joined the guerrilla forces in the mountains of Kurdistan.




From the outset, Comrade Sîrwan found a foundation for her personal and political development in the communal way of life of the guerrilla forces and the solidarity among comrades. During her ideological and military training, she deepened her engagement with women’s liberation ideology in particular. She questioned traditional gender roles and the social norms that restrict women’s self-determination.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/a2b60cf4_20261116113620_2026-11-17-behdinan-sirwan-qendil-sena-keremi-20-12-2024-zap-sehit-besdarbuyin-1.mp4










After completing her training, she took on duties in the Qendîl Mountains. She put her theoretical knowledge into practice and, through her eagerness to learn, discipline, and tireless dedication, developed into an experienced fighter of the Free Women’s Troops (YJA Star). Her comrades valued her modesty, sincerity, and unwavering stance against patriarchal ways of thinking and behaving.




However, Comrade Sîrwan never considered her training complete. She wanted to further develop her ideological and military skills and therefore specialized in various military fields, particularly as a sniper. In the face of increasing attacks by the Turkish army on the Medya Defense Zones, she insisted on taking on responsibilities in the regions where fighting was particularly intense.




When the Turkish army expanded its attacks on Metîna, Zap, and Avaşîn, Comrade Sîrwan strongly advocated taking part in the defense of these areas. She eventually went to the western front of the Zap region, where she joined the resistance against the occupation. In the clashes there, she combined her military skills with her conviction that the struggle for Kurdistan’s freedom was inseparably linked to women’s liberation. Her determination, willingness to take on difficult tasks, and unwavering commitment to the principles of women’s liberation made her a valued comrade-in-arms.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/b800975f_20261116113528_2026-11-17-behdinan-sirwan-qendil-sena-keremi-20-12-2024-zap-sehit-nirxandin-1.mp4










Comrade Sîrwan also participated in the defense against Turkish army attacks in the Sergelê resistance area. She prepared meticulously for military confrontations and carried out her duties with determination and a strong sense of responsibility. On December 20, 2024, our comrade Sîrwan Qendîl fell in an enemy attack on the Sergelê resistance area on the Şehîd Delîl Front in western Zap.




Through her sincere personality, her close bonds with her comrades, and her unwavering commitment to women’s liberation ideology, she left a lasting legacy. She continued the freedom struggle for which her cousin Sîrwan Merîwan had already given his life, carrying forward his legacy with great determination. We will preserve the memory of our comrade Sîrwan Qendîl and continue her struggle for the freedom of Kurdistan and women’s liberation. We extend our heartfelt condolences to her esteemed patriotic family, the people of Eastern Kurdistan, and the entire patriotic people of Kurdistan.




Hewrê Kemanger




Our comrade Hewrê Kemanger grew up in Merîwan in a patriotic family that preserved its Kurdish language, culture, and social values and passed them on to the next generation. He attended schools run by the Iranian regime for eight years. At a young age, he began working alongside his father to help support his family. Through his hard work, sincerity, and willingness to help others, he earned the respect and appreciation of those around him.




Comrade Hewrê developed an early interest in the social and political struggles of our people. During the Newroz celebrations in 2010, he was arrested by Iranian forces and held in custody for three days. The repression and torture he endured during this period deepened his understanding of the nature of the Iranian regime and reinforced his opposition to its policies of oppression.




In 2012, Comrade Hewrê became more closely acquainted with the Kurdish freedom movement. His engagement with its political and ideological foundations, as well as the guerrilla forces’ struggle against the occupying forces, left a deep impression on him. The martyrs of the Revolutionary People’s War and their commitment to the freedom of Kurdistan particularly strengthened his determination to assume responsibility himself. In 2013, he joined the guerrilla forces in the mountains of Kurdistan. He received his initial military and ideological training in the Qendîl region. There, he became familiar with the communal way of life of the guerrilla forces and the solidarity among comrades. In this environment, he found the values of sincerity, mutual responsibility, and solidarity that he had been seeking.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/f98c8689_20261116113649_2026-11-17-behdinan-hewre-kemanger-salim-muradi-09-06-2020-zap-sehit-sicil-1.mp4










During his training, he engaged intensively with the philosophy of Leader Apo and further developed his ideological and military skills. After completing his basic training, he took on various duties within the guerrilla forces. In 2015, Comrade Hewrê continued his military training at the Şehîd Mehmet Goyî Operations School. There, he specialized in military operations and prepared to assume responsibility amid increasingly intense fighting.




The genocidal attacks by the Islamic State (ISIS) terrorist organization against the Yazidi population of Shengal had caused great outrage among Comrade Hewrê. He therefore insisted on taking part in the defense of Shengal. That same year, he went to the region and joined the resistance against ISIS. He participated in numerous operations, helped defend the Yazidi population, and used his military skills to combat the genocidal attacks. Through his determination, courage, and level-headed approach even under difficult conditions, he earned the respect of his comrades.




After completing his duties in Shengal, Hewrê Kemanger returned to the Medya Defense Zones in 2018. He initially spent some time in Gare. However, in view of the increasing attacks by the Turkish army, he sought to be transferred to one of the regions where fighting was particularly intense. That same year, he went to Zap and participated in the resistance against the occupation. He applied the experience he had gained during the defense of Shengal to his new responsibilities. He distinguished himself through his dedication, military experience, and close bonds with his comrades.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/7ef31a66_20261116113743_2026-11-17-behdinan-hewre-kemanger-salim-muradi-09-06-2020-zap-sehit-nirxandin-1.mp4










On June 9, 2020, our comrade Hewrê Kemanger fell in an enemy attack in the Şehîd Rustem area of Zap. We remember this sincere and determined son of Merîwan and Eastern Kurdistan with great respect and deep gratitude. Through his commitment to the defense of Shengal and his subsequent struggle against the Turkish occupation attacks, he left behind a significant legacy. We will preserve the memory of Hewrê Kemanger and all our fallen comrades and continue their struggle for a free Kurdistan and the freedom of Leader Apo. We extend our heartfelt condolences to his esteemed patriotic and hardworking family and to the entire patriotic people of Kurdistan.




Sîrwan Zirêbar




Our comrade Sîrwan Zirêbar, who was also born in Merîwan, grew up in a patriotic family belonging to the long-established Caf tribe. His family maintained close ties to Kurdish identity, language, and culture and instilled in him a strong sense of national consciousness from childhood. He attended schools run by the Iranian regime for ten years. During this time, he became increasingly aware of the state’s assimilation policies and recognized that the education system was intended to alienate Kurdish children from their language and identity. His opposition to these policies grew stronger with each passing year. After leaving school, he worked alongside his family in vineyards and gardens. In this way, he learned the value of hard work at an early age and developed a deep attachment to his homeland and the land on which he had grown up.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/2702bed6_20261116113839_2026-11-17-behdinan-sirwan-zirebar-ednan-tazik-09-06-2020-zap-sehit-nirxandin-1.mp4










Through his family’s patriotic stance, Comrade Sîrwan became acquainted with the Kurdish freedom movement at a young age. He was particularly impressed by the guerrilla forces’ willingness to make sacrifices and their commitment to resisting attacks against our people. He came to believe that he, too, had to assume responsibility in the freedom struggle. During this period, he engaged intensively with the philosophy of Leader Apo and deepened his political and ideological commitment to our movement. In 2016, as attacks against our people and the Turkish state’s policies of annihilation reached a new level of intensity, Comrade Sîrwan decided to take up the armed struggle for freedom. He joined the guerrilla forces in the mountains of Kurdistan and began his initial military and ideological training in the Qendîl Mountains.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/4e6ee8d6_20261116113858_2026-11-17-behdinan-sirwan-zirebar-ednan-tazik-09-06-2020-zap-sehit-sicil-1.mp4










The modest attitude of the guerrilla fighters, their sincere relationships with one another, and their communal way of life left a deep impression on him. He quickly adapted to military discipline and the difficult conditions of life in the mountains. At the same time, he used his training to deepen his ideological knowledge and free himself from individualistic ways of thinking and behaving. His close bonds with his comrades and his experiences of communal life filled him with such enthusiasm that he often regretted not having joined the guerrilla forces earlier. He sought to make up for this perceived lost time through his tireless participation in revolutionary life and his willingness to take on new responsibilities.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/8711be95_20261116113926_2026-11-17-behdinan-sirwan-zirebar-ednan-tazik-09-06-2020-zap-sehit-perwerde-1.mp4










After completing his training, Comrade Sîrwan initially remained in Qendîl. There, he participated in the construction of military positions, the development of infrastructure, and, in particular, the construction of defensive tunnels. He carried out these tasks with great care and dedication, gaining valuable practical experience in the process. He subsequently sought to further develop his military skills and familiarize himself with new forms of guerrilla warfare. To this end, he continued his training at the Şehîd Mahir Academy, where he received specialized training in targeted military operations.




After completing this training, Comrade Sîrwan went to the Zap region in 2018, one of the main centers of resistance against the Turkish army’s attacks. There, he actively participated in military confrontations and put his previously acquired knowledge into practice. Alongside his military duties, he continued working on the expansion of defensive tunnels and took part in the communal tasks of everyday guerrilla life. For him, armed resistance, practical work, and responsibility toward his comrades were inseparably linked.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/ba72a7a7_20261116113948_2026-11-17-behdinan-sirwan-zirebar-ednan-tazik-09-06-2020-zap-sehit-besdarbuyin-1.mp4










Through his sincere, modest, and supportive personality, Comrade Sîrwan earned the respect and appreciation of his fellow comrades. He never shied away from difficult tasks and was always ready to assume responsibility wherever his skills and efforts were needed.




On June 9, 2020, our comrade Sîrwan Zirêbar fell in an enemy attack in the Şehîd Rustem area of Zap. Through his determination, tireless efforts, and unwavering commitment to the values of the freedom struggle, he earned a lasting place in our movement. We will preserve his memory and renew our pledge to continue the struggle of our fallen comrades for a free Kurdistan and the freedom of Abdullah Öcalan. We extend our heartfelt condolences to his esteemed patriotic family from the Caf tribe in Merîwan and to the entire patriotic people of Kurdistan.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/c815143b_20261116114014_2026-11-17-behdinan-sirwan-zirebar-ednan-tazik-09-06-2020-zap-sehit-perwerde-sekvan-1.mp4










Serxwebûn Hewraman




Our comrade Serxwebûn Hewraman grew up in a patriotic family belonging to the Geyî tribe, based in Merîwan. His family maintained close ties to the Kurdish language, culture, and national values of our people. In this environment, he developed a strong awareness of his identity and the social conditions in his homeland from an early age.




Comrade Serxwebûn attended educational institutions run by the Iranian regime for 14 years and completed a university degree in building services engineering. After graduating, he worked in his profession and gained practical experience as an engineer. At the same time, he critically examined the Iranian state’s policies toward our people. He did not want to place his technical and scientific knowledge at the service of the colonial system but instead sought to use it for Kurdistan’s freedom struggle.




After his older brother joined the guerrilla forces, Comrade Serxwebûn began studying our movement and its political and ideological foundations more intensively. The way of life of the guerrilla fighters, their willingness to make sacrifices, and the solidarity among comrades deeply impressed him. He developed a desire to join the guerrilla forces himself and assume responsibility in the freedom struggle.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/2a7694ad_20261116114101_2026-11-17-behdinan-serwebun-hewraman-sahid-edwayi-05-09-2022-sehit-sicil-1.mp4










Initially, however, he participated in the activities of our local militia structures. These duties required a high degree of discipline, responsibility, and secrecy. Comrade Serxwebûn carried them out with great care and made an important contribution to the organization of our movement. The genocidal attacks against our people in Rojava and Shengal strengthened his resolve to expand his involvement in the struggle and participate directly in the defense of Kurdistan. In 2017, he finally joined the guerrilla forces in the mountains of Kurdistan.




Having already established close ties with the freedom movement during his work within the militia structures, he quickly adapted to the communal way of life of the guerrilla forces. The difficult conditions of life in the mountains posed no obstacle to him. Rather, he regarded them as an opportunity to further develop his character and put his abilities at the service of their shared goals. During his ideological and military training, Comrade Serxwebûn deepened his understanding of the philosophy of Leader Apo. He engaged intensively with the principles of communal life and sought to overcome individualistic ways of thinking and behaving. After completing his training, he took on various duties in the Qendîl Mountains.




Over the following two years, he participated in numerous projects aimed at further developing military defense structures. Particular emphasis was placed on tunnel construction, which had become a central element of the new approach to guerrilla warfare. Comrade Serxwebûn was able to apply the knowledge he had acquired during his engineering studies directly to this work. His technical expertise, practical approach, and willingness to assume responsibility even under difficult conditions made him an important contributor to these efforts.




As the Turkish army intensified its attacks on the Medya Defense Zones, Comrade Serxwebûn pressed to be transferred to one of the regions where fighting was particularly intense. Given his military skills, experience, and determination, his request was eventually granted. He went to Zap, where resistance against Turkish military operations was increasingly concentrated. There, he took on duties in the Şikefta Birîndara area and participated in the expansion of defensive tunnels. He applied the experience he had previously gained in Qendîl under conditions of direct military confrontation.




Comrade Serxwebûn did not limit himself to planning or providing technical guidance for the work. Alongside his comrades, he participated directly in tunnel construction, working with a pickaxe and shovel and helping to expand the defensive positions despite limited resources. With great perseverance, he prepared the area for the anticipated attacks and supported the implementation of new forms of guerrilla warfare.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/0de6c0af_20261116114136_2026-11-17-behdinan-serwebun-hewraman-sahid-edwayi-05-09-2022-sehit-nirxandin-1.mp4










When the Turkish army launched its large-scale attacks in 2021 and further expanded them in 2022, Comrade Serxwebûn was among the guerrilla fighters who resisted in Şikefta Birîndara. He participated in numerous military operations and assumed important responsibilities both in defending the positions and maintaining the infrastructure. Despite the continued attacks involving fighter jets, armed drones, artillery, and heavy bombs, he continued his work alongside his comrades. Drawing on his technical knowledge and military experience, he helped maintain the defensive positions and sustain the resistance under extremely difficult conditions.




When the Turkish army was unable to break the resistance in Şikefta Birîndara, it resorted to prohibited methods of warfare. It systematically used chemical warfare agents and thermobaric weapons against our positions. Even under these conditions, Comrade Serxwebûn remained resolute and continued the resistance alongside his comrades. On September 5, 2022, our comrade Serxwebûn Hewraman fell in a chemical weapons attack by the Turkish army on the Şikefta Birîndara resistance area in Zap.




Through his sincerity, modesty, and tireless efforts, he earned the deep respect of his comrades. He combined his scientific and technical knowledge with his political convictions and placed his abilities entirely at the service of the freedom struggle. In doing so, he became a role model for his fellow comrades. We will preserve the memory of Serxwebûn Hewraman and renew our pledge to continue the struggle of our fallen comrades for a free Kurdistan and the freedom of Abdullah Öcalan. We extend our heartfelt condolences to his esteemed patriotic family from the Geyî tribe in Merîwan and to the entire patriotic people of Kurdistan.




Serkeft Hewramî




Our comrade Serkeft Hewramî was born in a village in the Jawaro region of Hewraman, an area with a long tradition of resistance. He grew up in a patriotic family that maintained close ties to the Kurdish language, culture, and the national and social values of our people. This environment shaped his identity and his awareness of Kurdistan’s history and aspirations for freedom from an early age.




Serkeft attended schools run by the Iranian regime for ten years. Even during his school years, he critically examined the state’s education policies, which were aimed at denying and assimilating Kurdish identity. After leaving school, he worked in various jobs to help support his family. Through his hard work, modesty, and willingness to help others, he earned the respect and appreciation of those around him.




In his homeland, many people actively participated in the Kurdish freedom struggle. People from his immediate community had also lost their lives in this struggle. These experiences shaped Comrade Serkeft’s political consciousness and strengthened his desire to assume responsibility for the freedom and a dignified future of our people. He began to study the Kurdish freedom movement and the paradigm of Leader Apo intensively. Through this process, he came to believe that the PKK was a leading force in the struggle for Kurdistan’s freedom and national unity. He was particularly impressed by the guerrillas’ willingness to make sacrifices and their communal way of life, characterized by mutual responsibility.




Comrade Serkeft developed a desire to join the guerrilla forces himself and participate directly in the freedom struggle. However, various circumstances and obstacles initially prevented him from fulfilling this decision. As the Turkish army expanded its attacks on Rojava and other parts of Kurdistan, his determination grew stronger. He regarded the military operations as attacks on the achievements our people had secured through great sacrifices. He was convinced that the best way to preserve his family’s revolutionary legacy and honor the memory of the martyrs was to join the freedom struggle himself.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/512180a1_20261116114217_2026-11-17-behdinan-serkeft-hewrami-zana-semedi-19-10-2022-sehit-sicil-1.mp4










In 2019, Comrade Serkeft finally put his decision into action and went to the mountains of Kurdistan to join the guerrilla forces. He received his initial ideological and military training in the Qendîl Mountains. The communal way of life of the guerrilla forces and the relationships among comrades, based on solidarity, mutual responsibility, and selfless dedication, left a deep impression on him. Comrade Serkeft participated in communal life with great enthusiasm and engaged intensively with the ideological foundations of our movement. He sought to overcome individualistic ways of thinking and behaving and to further develop his character in accordance with the Apoist philosophy of life. At the same time, he acquired the military knowledge and skills required for his future duties.




After successfully completing his training, he initially remained in Qendîl for a short time, where he took on various duties. However, when the Turkish army launched its large-scale attacks on Xakurke, Comrade Serkeft pressed to be transferred to this particularly heavily contested area. Through his determination and persistent efforts, he convinced his comrades to grant his request. He went to Xakurke and joined the resistance against Turkish military operations there.




Comrade Serkeft participated in numerous military operations against the Turkish army. He distinguished himself through his courage, determination, and willingness to assume responsibility even under difficult conditions. He put the knowledge he had acquired during his training into military practice. He also took on numerous responsibilities in communal life and participated in daily tasks with great dedication. His sincerity, hard work, and spirit of solidarity made him a valued companion among his comrades. He combined his military determination with a deep sense of connection to the people with whom he lived and fought.










https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/77753c7d_20261116114241_2026-11-17-behdinan-serkeft-hewrami-zana-semedi-19-10-2022-sehit-detay-1.mp4










On October 19, 2022, our comrade Serkeft Hewramî fell in an enemy attack in the Ermûş area of Xakurke, where he continued to resist until the very end. Through his sincere personality, determined attitude, and unwavering commitment to the values of the freedom struggle, he earned a lasting place in our movement. He had joined the struggle with the aim of achieving a free Kurdistan and securing the freedom of Leader Apo, and remained faithful to this conviction until his death.




We renew the pledge we made to Serkeft Hewramî and all our fallen comrades: We will preserve their memory and continue their struggle until their goals are achieved. We extend our heartfelt condolences to his esteemed patriotic family from Jawaro, the people of Eastern Kurdistan, and the entire patriotic people of Kurdistan.

title: DEM Party calls for timetable for parliamentary monitoring commission
content:
The Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) is calling for a binding timetable for the establishment of a parliamentary monitoring commission as part of the peace and democratization process. At a press conference at the party’s headquarters, spokesperson Ayşegül Doğan criticized the fact that it remained unclear when the commission would begin its work despite talks between Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş and the political parties.




Following the talks last week, Kurtulmuş had announced that the commission would be established “in the coming days.” Doğan described this statement as insufficient: “Instead of vague statements, a timetable should have been presented long ago. What are they waiting for to complete the preparations? Why is there a delay? There is nothing left to wait for.”




The DEM Party spokesperson demanded that the commission’s working procedures, responsibilities, and roadmap be made public. She also said it was necessary to clarify the political framework under which the parties would cooperate within the commission. She noted that the delays were also affecting coordination between the legislative and executive branches.




Call for the participation of all parties




Doğan emphasized that all parliamentary groups must be represented on the monitoring commission, and that broad political participation was essential to the success of the peace process. In this context, she criticized the decision by Yeni Party Chair Özgür Özel not to nominate any members to the commission. During the work of the National Commission for Solidarity, Brotherhood and Democracy, he had declined to participate in the delegation visiting Abdullah Öcalan. This was compounded by votes against the framework law.




“Now comes the decision not to participate in the monitoring commission either. It creates the impression that they want to avoid being perceived as supporters of the process at all costs. This does not reflect well on them,” Doğan stated. She stressed that the demand for democratization was legitimate and necessary but must not lead political forces to distance themselves from the peace process. Peace and democratization were inseparably linked, she underlined.




Doğan warned that the Yeni Party’s stance could widen the gap between the party and the Kurdish people. “The debate must not be reduced to party-political majorities and tactical calculations. We are in a process that must rise above such calculations and in which potential pitfalls must be identified in time. To end this war that has lasted for 50 years, everyone must be at the table. We call for the participation of all parties.”




“Sick prisoners must not be left to die”




Another major focus of the press conference was the situation of seriously ill prisoners. Doğan expressed her support for the indefinite vigil outside the Turkish Ministry of Justice, which is demanding the release of sick prisoners and guaranteed access to medical care.




She recalled the recent death of political prisoner Tuncer Sağlam and criticized the fact that applications for release from prison and suspension of sentence had gone unanswered. “If it is possible to save a person’s life but a decision is made not to do so, then that is a political decision,” Doğan said. She also cited the cases of Evin Zapsu, who is imprisoned in Kayseri-Bünyan Women’s Prison and has stage IV cancer, and Newroz Bozkurt, who is being held in Sincan Women’s Prison and suffers from chronic leukemia.




“The imprisonment of seriously ill people under prison conditions must end. We will not allow the right to life to be subjected to arbitrary administrative decisions, political calculations, and arbitrary practices. We support the sit-in protest and will stand in solidarity with the families until the very end. For us, this is a matter of rights and justice.”




Criticism of appointed trustees and political bans




Doğan also condemned an appeals court’s decision to uphold the 19-year-and-six-month prison sentence imposed on Sıddık Akış, the co-mayor of Hakkari. She pointed out that the ruling had been issued at a time when the legal foundations of the peace process were under discussion. The continued arrest and prosecution of Kurdish politicians, she argued, contradicted the stated goal of democratic reform. According to Doğan, what is needed is an expansion of the space for democratic politics rather than further restrictions.




The DEM Party spokesperson also criticized restrictions on access to media outlets and limitations on the use of the Kurdish language. She pointed out that the language issue was among the fundamental matters that needed to be addressed in the peace process. Doğan also spoke out against the ban on political activity imposed the previous day on ousted Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu and other politicians. “Instead of democratic political competition, we are witnessing an attempt to eliminate political opponents through judicial and administrative measures.”




Öcalan to coordinate Peace and Political Engagement Council




Regarding the planned Peace and Political Engagement Council, Doğan stated that its composition and working structure had not yet been finalized: “Neither the number of members nor their names have been determined. Politicians could also be included. However, preparations are already behind schedule,” Doğan said, calling for the council to begin its work without delay and for preparations to be made for a visit to the prison island of Imrali.




“We expect the Peace and Political Engagement Council to begin its work as soon as possible in the coming days and to be able to travel to Imrali. This is not merely a wish but an expression of our demand that the necessary preparations finally be completed.”




At the same time, Doğan made clear the role that her party believed Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan should assume within the council: “Of course, Mr. Öcalan must also be a member of this council as its coordinator – as the coordinator of the Peace and Political Engagement Council.”

title: New photo of Abdullah Öcalan released
content:
A new photo of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan, who is imprisoned on the Turkish prison island of Imrali, has been released. The photo was taken on October 9, 2026, during a family visit.




The photo was published on Wednesday by Ömer Öcalan, Abdullah Öcalan’s nephew and a member of parliament for the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party). The photo shows Abdullah Öcalan alongside his nephew Ömer Öcalan, his niece Havva Elçin, and his cousin Hacı Aydın Öcalan.

title: Women hold dialogue workshop in Qamishlo
content:
The workshop was attended by 300 participants, including members of women’s movements and organisations, as well as female intellectuals and politicians. Discussions focused on political and legal violence and the role of women in integration.




The declaration issued following the workshop highlighted the following points:




1. Guaranteeing women’s rights in the Syrian constitution and ensuring equality between women and men. No discrimination should be made on the basis of gender, nationality or religion, and women’s rights should be constitutionally guaranteed.




2. Guaranteeing women’s participation in legislative, executive, administrative and judicial institutions, ensuring that they are represented and have decision-making power at every level.




3. Guaranteeing education in the mother tongue in the constitution.




4. Fighting political and institutional violence against women, as well as taking a stand against policies of ignoring women. Women must be guaranteed the right to organise, express their opinions and participate in politics.




5. Protecting women from violence through laws and mechanisms. Ending domestic, social, economic and sexual violence, and punishing those who perpetrate violence against women. Ensuring women’s access to justice and protecting all women without discrimination.

title: Dr. Korkmaz: Turkey may pay a heavy price for military alliances
content:
Tensions between Iran and Israel, the new political landscape in Syria, escalating conflicts in Yemen and the Mecca Defence Pact are reshaping the balance of power in the Middle East. Relations between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Egypt and the Gulf states, the position of the Kurds in regional developments and the future of the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey are also among the major issues on the regional agenda.




Dr. Toros Korkmaz spoke to ANF about developments in the Middle East, regional power relations and the future of the peace process in Turkey.




'Power struggles in the Middle East bring both risks and opportunities'




Korkmaz said that the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey began at a time of continuing wars and power struggles in the Middle East, and that it could not be considered independently of the uncertainties created by these developments.




Korkmaz said: "Opportunities and risks do not emerge in isolation. This is actually a dialectical process. If we look at the peace process, a very serious perception of a security threat emerged in Israel following Hamas's attack on Israel on 7 October 2023. This prompted Israel to put its plan to reshape the Middle East into action. Following this plan, we witnessed the fragmentation of Syria, then the Israel-Iran war backed by the United States, and the direct involvement of the US in that war. The peace process came onto the agenda after all these developments. Frankly, I do not think such a peace process could have begun under the present circumstances if this environment of war had not emerged and if the Turkish government and state had not been aware of Israel's plan to reshape the Middle East. That is why I believe the 7 October attack was very important."




'A possible war with Iran will affect the process in Turkey'




Korkmaz said that the direction of the Kurdish question could change amid the ongoing armed conflicts in the Middle East, particularly the threat of war involving Iran. He warned of the risks arising from Turkey's reluctance to move the process forward.




Korkmaz also said: "Consider what would happen if Iran were severely weakened by the Iran-Israel war and entered a process of fragmentation. In that case, the possibility of Kurds in Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilat) gaining increasing autonomy would emerge. This would put pressure on Turkey. Under such circumstances, Turkey might decide to continue the peace process. However, a different picture could emerge if the current stalemate continues and the Turkish state concludes that Israel has reached the limits of its power and no longer has the capacity to advance further or reshape the Middle East. If such a perception develops within the Turkish state, there may be a tendency to freeze or slow down the peace process, or to limit reforms as much as possible.




Therefore, how the war ends, who emerges victorious and what kind of regional situation develops afterwards are extremely important. Will Iran fragment or remain intact? What are the limits of Israel's power? All these questions will be decisive."




'National consciousness and aspirations are growing among Kurds'




Korkmaz said that the war concerned not only Turkey and the Turkish state but also the development of Kurdish national consciousness throughout the conflict.




Korkmaz said: "National consciousness is growing among Kurds across all four parts of Kurdistan, in Syria, Iraq, Iran and Turkey. Kurds recognise that the Middle East has become a region engulfed in conflict and that they can survive this period only by strengthening unity and solidarity among themselves. I believe this is an important development.




The Kurdish dynamic must be taken into account. It cannot be ignored. Kurds are becoming increasingly aware of their national identity and are organising across all four parts of Kurdistan. What have we witnessed during this process? For example, for the first time, all Kurdish parties in Iran came together. Organisations that previously seemed incapable of coming together found common ground. In Turkey, particularly in Northern Kurdistan, there has also been a significant increase in national consciousness. At times when Kurdish rights were violated in Rojava and the region was under threat, Kurds mobilised not only in Turkey but also across Europe.




War creates existential conditions, and such circumstances can contribute positively to the development of national consciousness among peoples. I believe Kurdish national consciousness has developed more strongly during this war than in previous periods."




'The Mecca Pact could draw Turkey into conflicts'




Korkmaz warned that Turkey might feel compelled to enter alliances that could prove extremely costly, describing the Mecca Agreement as one such arrangement.




Korkmaz said: "Under this agreement, three countries, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey, form a military defence pact. However, this pact also carries numerous risks. From an external and superficial perspective, one might reach the following conclusion: Money will come from Saudi Arabia and the Gulf countries it leads, while Turkey possesses military technology. This would create a new market for Turkey, allowing it to sell military technology to the Gulf states. Pakistan, meanwhile, could provide support in the nuclear and military fields. That is the picture presented by a superficial assessment.




However, a closer examination reveals a different situation. Saudi Arabia is engaged on numerous fronts. It has a direct front in Yemen, another in Sudan and a front against Iran in the Gulf. It also has a front to the north, in Syria. In other words, we are talking about a power involved in conflicts and tensions in many places. Pakistan also faces problems on at least five different fronts. Moreover, Pakistan is one of the world's most authoritarian countries. Human rights activists there can be detained and imprisoned directly on terrorism charges.




Both Saudi Arabia and Pakistan are countries governed by authoritarian regimes where democracy is absent. At the same time, they are involved in conflicts and tensions with other countries."




'Turkey could pay a heavy military price'




Korkmaz warned that Turkey's participation in the Mecca Pact could oblige it to deploy troops to conflict zones. He said: "This could result in substantial loss of life. These are enormous risks. Indeed, as soon as the Mecca Agreement was signed, India strongly objected to Pakistan and declared that the agreement was directed against it. This aspect is also extremely important. Turkey could face heavy costs and be forced to deploy troops directly. While seeking to gain access to a market, it could suffer very serious casualties.




Secondly, the Mecca alliance also has a sectarian character. In its current form, it appears to be a Sunni alliance. It also involves positioning against Iran. We know that Iran supports various forces in the Middle East. The conflict in Yemen, Hezbollah in Lebanon and the confrontations with Israel must be considered in this context. If the war in Yemen intensifies in the future and the Houthis strengthen their position, Turkey could find itself confronting a bloc of forces linked to Iran. A conflict with Hezbollah or Iran could come onto the agenda. This would have extremely serious consequences."




'The Mecca Pact could become an agreement targeting Kurds'




Korkmaz said that Turkey's attempts to assume a role in the Middle East's power struggles, while disregarding the Kurds, carried major risks.




Korkmaz continued: "There is a fire burning somewhere, and you approach it with petrol as part of a military strategy. Instead of doing this, if Turkey reached an agreement with the Kurds, recognised their rights and became a genuinely democratic country in the region, it could achieve far greater gains than those it hopes to obtain through military alliances.




That is because Turkey could then be presented as an example of democracy in the Middle East. Consider another example. Would Turkey gain more economically, culturally and in every other field by joining the European Union and becoming part of it, or through military alliances with authoritarian regimes?Making peace with the Kurds and ensuring their democratic integration would also positively affect Turkey's relations with the West and the European Union.




We should also examine the provisions of the Mecca Pact. In particular, Article 5 provides for intelligence sharing against terrorist organisations. At first glance, this provision might appear reasonable. However, the Turkish state still regards the Rojava region, the Kurds of Rojava and the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) as terrorist entities. Likewise, the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), or what is now called the Kurdish Movement, is viewed in the same way. The Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK) in Iran is also designated a terrorist organisation.




Consequently, even if it is not explicitly stated, this agreement could involve an approach targeting the Kurds. This is an agreement between nation-states that prioritises the nation-state mentality. It is based on nation-state structures that disregard the peoples of the region, different beliefs and the pluralistic character of the Middle East.




Yet the Kurds are one of the strongest local forces in the region. Nevertheless, the nation-states in which they live can easily classify them as terrorist elements. The Mecca Agreement inherently carries this risk. It may have other benefits, but I believe the possibility of it becoming an agreement directed against the Kurds is more important. This dimension must be examined and discussed."




'

A ground operation against Iran would be risky'




Korkmaz also examined why Iran had not collapsed despite the interventions against it. He said: "The Iranian regime has managed to remain in power so far. One of the main reasons is that Iran is a very large country. It has approximately twice Turkey's population and territory. Geographically, the Zagros Mountains lie to the south, while the Alborz Mountains lie to the north. Iran is a protected region surrounded by these mountain ranges.




It has become clear that the regime cannot be overthrown through air strikes alone. That would require a major ground operation. Military experts say that occupying Iran by land would require at least 1.5 to 2 million troops. Even deploying a force of that size would not guarantee the operation's success. Such an undertaking would carry enormous risks. At present, there are no serious indications that Iran is about to collapse or fragment in the near future. This must be stated clearly.




This is where a major risk also emerges for Turkey. The United States could use the Mecca alliance as a justification for involving Turkey in a major ground operation against Iran. This is a possibility, and it represents a serious risk. What the Kurds need to do in this situation is pursue cautious and realistic politics. It would be wrong to adopt an approach such as, 'The Iranian regime will collapse soon, so let us launch an uprising for independence and freedom,' or 'We will act when the US and Israel give us the go-ahead.' Acting in this way could cause extremely serious harm.




As in Turkey, Kurds should push for democratic integration in Iran. They should be able to say to the Iranian state, 'You are under a major attack. Recognise our rights and establish a democratic system based on those rights.' That is because when democracy develops, the justification for external attacks also disappears. Where does the claimed legitimacy of attacks against Iran come from today? From the Iranian regime's theocratic and authoritarian character, its oppression of peoples and its refusal to recognise democratic rights. If Iran had a pluralistic, democratic and secular system, and had developed a model of governance similar to that of Rojava, these attacks would lose their legitimacy.




Therefore, what Kurds should do there is push for democratic integration rather than launch an uprising for independence at the instigation of the US and Israel. A wait-and-see approach may be an appropriate strategy for the Kurds. However, this must not mean remaining passive. They need to strengthen their organisations, struggle for democratic integration and increase pressure on the Iranian regime in this direction. That is what the Kurds should do."




'The Turkish state insists on a security-based approach to the process'




Toros Korkmaz said that achieving democratic integration through the ongoing process in Turkey would benefit the entire region. He stressed the importance of developing a pluralistic and democratic mentality and highlighted the value of Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan's warnings on this issue.




Korkmaz said: "Turning to the process in Turkey, unfortunately, we cannot see any progress at present. Realistically speaking, the process is not moving forward. The state has not managed to change its traditional statist and nationalist approach. It continues to view the Kurdish question entirely from a security-based perspective, treating it as a terrorism issue.




When we examine the statements of senior state representatives, the President and high-ranking bureaucrats, we see that the issue is still being described as a terrorism problem. The statements by presidential adviser Mehmet Uçum that the first four articles of the Constitution will not be changed also reflect this approach. The Kurdish question is still not being acknowledged as an issue of identity, culture and language. It has been reduced entirely to a terrorism issue.




The process is currently stuck. We cannot see any progress. What needs to be done at this point is to maintain pressure on the state to take steps. The Turkish state tradition is characterised by an unwillingness to act unless it faces pressure. Therefore, Kurds must express their demands for identity and language rights as strongly as possible and struggle alongside other democratic forces in Turkey by building the broadest possible organisations. This is the stage the process has reached.




However, it is the Turkish state that will suffer the consequences of this situation, and it is already doing so. This must also be said. The reason Turkey feels compelled to enter the Mecca Agreement is its failure to democratise internally. If Turkey had been able to democratise itself, it would not have had to assume military obligations that could come at such a heavy cost. However, because those governing the state do not have a sufficiently democratic mentality, have failed to develop a democratic approach and still do not understand this reality, they are exposing Turkey to enormous risks."

title: Women's Peace Monitoring Commission established in Istanbul
content:
The Women's Peace Monitoring and Follow-up Commission announced its establishment following preparatory meetings involving approximately 100 women.




The commission announced its establishment at a press conference held at the Kadın Zamanı Association. It aims to be represented on the Independent Monitoring Board to be established under the framework law adopted by Parliament. Representatives of women's organisations and many other women attended the meeting, where participants chanted the slogan "Jin, jiyan, azadî" (Woman, Life, Freedom).




The statement emphasised that lasting peace requires more than an end to conflict. It also involves confronting the past, uncovering the truth, ensuring justice and rebuilding society.




The statement drew attention to the impact of war, forced displacement and losses experienced across generations on women, stressing that women's equal participation and authority in decision-making mechanisms are fundamental to lasting peace.




The statement noted that women experience war and conflict in different ways, including imprisonment, poverty, male violence, labour exploitation and displacement, but that these experiences are often made invisible in peace processes. The commission stressed the need for independent monitoring of the process from a gender equality perspective.
