title: Evin Zapsu's lawyer: Evin is in severe pain and needs treatment
content:
The health condition of seriously ill prisoner Evin Zapsu, who is held at Kayseri Bünyan Women's Closed Prison and was diagnosed with cancer on 16 November, remains critical. Biopsy results and other medical examinations revealed stage four uterine cancer that has spread to other parts of her body. Despite repeated calls for her release, Evin Zapsu remains imprisoned.




Relatives of ill prisoners have called for their release outside the Ministry of Justice, while Evin Zapsu's lawyer, Berivan Çelik, spoke to ANF about her client's health and the latest developments.




'Evin is suffering from severe pain'




Berivan Çelik said that Evin Zapsu remained in good spirits despite trying to conceal the pain, swelling and physical changes. Çelik said that doctors had informed Evin Zapsu, who was diagnosed with stage four uterine cancer with metastases, that she urgently needed surgery. She warned that further delays in treatment could leave her client dependent on others for care.




The lawyer said that she met Evin Zapsu face to face at the prison last Tuesday and witnessed her deteriorating health firsthand.




Despite taking two strong painkillers, Evin Zapsu was visibly suffering from severe pain and had significant abdominal swelling and other physical changes. Çelik said that her client remained in good spirits but was trying to conceal her suffering.




Berivan Çelik said: "Although she had taken two strong painkillers before coming to our meeting, it was very clear that she was in pain, even though she tried not to show it. Nevertheless, her spirits were high and she was smiling. She believed that even if her test results were bad, she would be able to overcome the illness without too much difficulty."




Report concludes that she can remain in prison




Berivan Çelik said that an earlier medical assessment had concluded that her client could remain in prison. Three days after they submitted a request for the postponement of her sentence and her release, Evin Zapsu was taken to Kayseri City Hospital, where a medical board prepared a report.




Çelik said that the report concluded that Evin Zapsu was fit to remain in prison, while subsequent biopsy results revealed the severity of her illness.




Çelik also said: "Three days after we first requested the postponement of her sentence and her release, Evin was taken to Kayseri City Hospital. A medical board report was prepared at the hospital, and the report issued last Monday concluded that she could remain in prison. However, the biopsy results revealed stage four uterine cancer with metastases.




We therefore submitted another application today. We have not yet received a written response to our previous request. No decision approving or rejecting our application has been communicated to us."




'The masses have spread to her chest and armpits'




Berivan Çelik also referred to radiological imaging and CT scan results, saying that her client's health had deteriorated since the first scans were carried out in August.




Çelik said that masses initially detected in the abdominal area had spread over time and that new masses had developed.




Çelik also said: "The initial radiological scans showed masses only in her abdomen. She told us that these masses had gradually spread upwards towards her chest and that new masses had begun to appear in her armpits. We have the radiological images, CT scans, their reports and the biopsy results.




When we compare the reports from August with her current condition, we can see that the masses have increased considerably and are causing much more pain."




Berivan Çelik said that the doctor who examined her client had told her that she urgently needed surgery to remove the masses. She explained that following the initial pathology results, she and Evin Zapsu's family had consulted an oncology specialist on the basis of the scans taken in August.




Although the specialist provided a verbal opinion, they were unable to obtain a written assessment. Following the biopsy results, they submitted a new application.




Çelik said that they attached the biopsy results to their second petition and stressed that treatment must begin immediately.




'Treatment is not possible under prison conditions'




Berivan Çelik also described the health problems her client faces in prison, saying that the cold conditions force her to sleep with hot-water bottles and that she spends most of her time in bed because of the pain.




The lawyer said that Zapsu's hospital visits generally resulted in little more than the administration of painkillers and added: "Evin told me that the prison was very cold and that she constantly had to lie down with hot-water bottles. She is also distressed by having to remain in bed and needing others to look after her. She tries to meet her own needs and makes an effort not to become dependent on anyone. 




Evin is taken to hospital when she requests it, but she is only admitted for outpatient consultations at the district state hospital or the city hospital. These visits generally involve only short-term treatment, such as painkillers."




'Treatment must begin immediately'




Berivan Çelik expressed concern about Evin Zapsu's health, stressing that despite her positive spirits during their meeting, the severity of her pain was unmistakable.




Çelik stressed that treatment must begin without further delay and concluded: "Evin was in very good spirits, but I witnessed her condition firsthand. It was obvious that she was suffering from severe pain. No matter how high her spirits were, it was extremely difficult for her to cope with that pain. She was doing everything she could to avoid showing it.




Her abdomen was severely swollen. There was visible redness, bruising and swelling associated with the pain. I witnessed all of this myself during our meeting. If her treatment does not begin as soon as possible, her condition will become much worse."

title: Janet Biehl: Democratic integration should guide the peace process
content:
American writer and social ecology thinker Janet Biehl, in an assessment she wrote on Abdullah Öcalan’s 27 February 2025 Call for Peace and a Democratic Society, emphasised the importance of democratic and legal steps for advancing the peace process in Turkey.




Statements and letters prepared as part of an international solidarity campaign launched with the participation of 97 intellectuals will be published as an English-language e-book by Daraja Press.




Janet Biehl’s foreword to the book, entitled “The Call for Peace and a Democratic Society”, was also conveyed to the Imrali Delegation.




In her article, Janet Biehl said that the Framework Law adopted by Parliament was of vital importance for advancing the process. She said that, following confirmation by the National Security Council of the PKK’s disarmament steps, the way could be paved for the reintegration into social life of political prisoners and some PKK members living abroad.




However, Janet Biehl emphasised that, alongside the implementation of the legal framework, additional confidence-building measures were also necessary. title: Kalkan: The women's freedom movement provides leadership to the entire struggle
content:
Duran Kalkan, a member of the Abdullah Öcalan Academy of Social Sciences, gave a lengthy interview to Medya Haber TV.




In the third and last part of this lengthy interview, he spoke about the importance of the women's movement, the PKK and the international situation.




Part one of the interview can be read 

here

, and the second 

here

.




I

t seems that there are people around the world raising their voices against this situation. Developments are taking place in this direction. The left has returned to power in Brazil. In Serbia, the side supported by the student movement came to power. Trump also lost. There are protests on the streets of Europe every day. How should we interpret these developments in the context of your latest assessment?




Recently, I have been thinking about certain things. Why have they destroyed Iran and Ukraine to such an extent? They also destroyed Syria. I remember the period when efforts were being made to develop Syria. A great deal of capital had been invested, and construction was taking place. This is the nature of the system. It destroys everything and then creates new business opportunities for itself through reconstruction. Naturally, while reconstruction takes place, the owners of capital add billions to their existing billions. They exploit people to such an extent and make enormous profits. Soon, for example, the reconstruction of Iran and Ukraine will begin. The monopolies will profit. They will make unprecedented profits from rebuilding Ukraine. New weapons will also be manufactured to replace those used in its destruction, and the monopolies of the arms industry will profit as well. This situation demonstrates more clearly than anything else the nature of the existing system, the system of power and the state, and the point it has reached under capitalist modernity. It is a system capable of launching even more severe attacks. Its internal contradictions and conflicts have become so deep.




Their greed for profit is so powerful that they are prepared to carry out every kind of attack to make more money and seize what others possess. Do you know what frightens them? Two things. The first is the fear of the revolutionary struggle of the peoples. They fear that if they fight among themselves, society might take advantage of the situation, develop consciousness, organise itself and enter into a revolutionary democratic struggle. They fear that an alternative capable of overthrowing them might emerge. That is their first fear. The October Revolution of 1917 instilled this fear in them. Earlier revolutionary attempts also did so. Many revolutionary developments throughout the twentieth century reinforced it. Today, they calculate this possibility every day. They live in fear. The second thing they fear is the weapons they have created. For example, we have been saying that the Third World War has been continuing for 30 or 35 years. It is not as intense or decisive in military terms as the First World War. Nor is it like the Second World War. Why? Because it cannot be. They cannot conduct the Third World War in that way. If they did, those launching the attacks would not only destroy their opponents but also destroy themselves.




The weapons they would use have reached a level where they threaten to destroy nature, the Earth, humanity, all living beings and the planet itself. That is the point we have reached. It is this fear that prevents them from escalating the war further. Some people say, "The military dimension is weak. These are preparations for the Third World War. The Third World War will come." The Third World War is already taking place. As we say in Kurdish to such people, "Rojbaş", meaning "Good morning!" It has been going on for 30 or 35 years. There will not be a war like the First or Second World War. That will not happen. Anyone who attempts such a thing would have to be considered completely insane. It would lead humanity towards extinction. Recently, people who do not seem entirely rational have risen towards positions of power. Naturally, humanity has experienced great fear in many areas. That is what was actually described as the rise of the right. There is no such thing as simply the rise of the right. What is rising is this danger. The system of capitalist modernity has reached that point. For the time being, they are still exercising some restraint. We should recognise that. But nobody really knows how long this can continue.




'We must resist this system'




The issues we have mentioned are connected to war. That is why I am raising them. They are connected to the war that has continued for 35 years. Its centre is the Middle East. The war between Iran and the United States and Israel continues. It continues at a low intensity. It has not stopped. There are claims that it will expand and that attacks will increase. We do not know what will happen. Ukraine was also a very important area between Asia and Europe. It was a northern energy corridor, an alternative to the route south of the Mediterranean. They acted to cut off that route. In the south, meanwhile, the war continues in the Middle East. Developments around the world are connected to this. The politics of war that threaten humanity have genuinely suffered a setback in recent elections. This is one dimension through which these developments should be assessed. The elections in Israel and the United States can be interpreted in this way. Developments stretching from Brazil to Serbia also show that democratic left-wing forces have become more effective. These forces exist, and similar developments can be seen in many other areas.




In Germany, the Left Party also won in Berlin. They are trying to prevent it from taking power. The existing state treats democratic, left-wing and socialist forces in a manner similar to its treatment of the fascist right-wing movement. But the main response came from young people. It began in France and spread to Italy, the Netherlands, Germany and everywhere else. It appealed to all sections of society. These were university students and secondary school students. What is particularly interesting is that they turned resistance into a social movement. They extended their leadership to other sections of society. They demonstrated something important: there will always be people who resist this system. No matter how extensively special warfare policies are employed, no matter what measures are taken to prevent different sections of society from opposing the system, some people will still break through that barrier, overcome special warfare and resist the system, raising the banner of resistance. The current situation has demonstrated this. I would like to make one final point on this subject. There are many issues that deserve further assessment and discussion.




'Left-wing and democratic forces are not doing enough'




These events, the developments we have discussed, have taught us something. In reality, it is not that there is some unstoppable rise of the right or that society is incapable of recognising what the forces of capital and the capitalist system are doing. We should not simply say, "They work very hard, their words and actions gain support in society, and that is why they win elections and threaten to come to power in Europe." What should we say instead? The truth is that left-wing and democratic forces are not working hard enough. They are insufficiently organised. We must recognise our own shortcomings. Those who call themselves democrats and socialists must engage in self-criticism. They are not doing enough to raise society's awareness. They are not sufficiently connected to society; they have become detached from it. They do not go among the people. They are too rigid and dogmatic. They cannot convince people or inspire confidence. They have almost reached a point where they operate within the existing system.




This is a very bad situation. The elections demonstrated it, and the resistance of young people demonstrated it as well. If there were genuinely a correct understanding, effective organisation and a determined struggle, the system of capitalist modernity could be exposed everywhere. An alternative democratic society system and the struggle for a democratic society could develop everywhere, gain supporters and become a mass movement. What is needed, therefore, is correct consciousness, a correct programme, appropriate strategies and tactics, and, of course, courageous and self-sacrificing efforts. If those who call themselves intellectuals, politicians and artists, those who claim to be the pioneers, the spirit and the consciousness of these societies, of the people and the oppressed, fulfil their duties and responsibilities, everything can develop successfully.




The anti-capitalist struggle can develop effectively everywhere, overcome capitalism and bring it to an end. In fact, capitalism has survived longer than it should have. It should never have reached this point. A hundred years ago, at the beginning of the twentieth century, revolutionaries said that prolonging its existence would be a catastrophe. It should already have been overcome. It survived for another century, and those responsible for creating an alternative, including socialist forces, bear significant responsibility for this. If they recognise and understand this and successfully fulfil their responsibilities as pioneers, it will be possible to overcome a system that threatens nature, society and humanity through such devastating warfare. Our call is therefore to develop this consciousness and struggle more strongly in every sphere.




You drew attention to the Dersim massacre. Of course, in response to these attacks, a major struggle was launched under the leadership of the PKK in 1978, and the values you have highlighted were created through the sacrifice of martyrs. As we approach its 48th anniversary, how should we understand this historical reality, and how should we assess its significance?




Yes, this is something we have always emphasised. The PKK is a movement of leadership and martyrs. What does this mean? It is not simply propaganda. It has a meaning and value rooted in real historical experience.




What it means is this: from its smallest steps to its greatest achievements, from its very first words to the entirety of its thought and action, everything was brought into being under the leadership of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan]. Leader Apo's creative thinking, labour, efforts and will made all these developments possible. Leader Apo became a leader through struggle, hard work and the creation of progress. It did not happen because someone simply bestowed such a title upon him. Nor was it a matter of assigning him a particular position. It did not happen behind a desk either. Starting from nothing, he carried out the work and struggle that gave rise to some of the most meaningful and significant developments in history. Through resistance everywhere — in the country, abroad and in İmralı prison — he developed and brought forth the reality of leadership. This must be properly understood. The reality of leadership is the greatest value created by the PKK and through the PKK's struggle. It has addressed the most significant deficiency of the Kurdish people.




Today, this has given rise to a development that extends beyond the borders of Kurdistan and meets a need felt by all oppressed peoples. The reality of leadership has truly become the source of intellectual and problem-solving power that points the way towards the liberation of all oppressed peoples.




The Kurds know this well. They have understood it and embraced it. We believe this will always remain the case. From one generation to the next, Kurdish youth will understand this value more deeply and comprehensively. They will defend it more strongly and follow and implement the truth of leadership with greater success.




Leader Apo said, "The PKK is the Party of Martyrs." He stated that the martyrs exist and live on in the form of the PKK. He described the PKK as the embodiment of the memory of Haki Karer. Indeed, from its very first steps up until the decision to end its organisational existence, every development took place along the line of martyrdom. It was created through struggle along this line. It was built through the sacrifice of martyrs and the shedding of blood. We are not talking about hundreds, nor thousands, but tens of thousands. And these martyrs are not exclusively men. Women took the lead in this struggle. Women demonstrated the greatest determination in fighting. They did so in the mountains, in prison and through social work. In this respect, the PKK became a movement defined by the reality of its martyrs.




Indeed, at the congress held in May 2025, where the PKK's organisational existence was formally dissolved, the congress entrusted the values it had created to the people. Above all, it entrusted the reality of leadership and martyrdom to the people on this basis. It entrusted these values to the martyrs. It said: "Understand the line of leadership and martyrdom correctly. Always uphold it. Never abandon or break away from this line."




This was very important. This process is continuing. Over the past three months, hundreds of comrades who had fallen as martyrs during the previous five or six years but whose deaths had not yet been publicly announced were declared as martyrs in Bakur (North Kurdistan), Başur (South Kurdistan), Rojhilat (East Kurdistan), Rojava (West Kurdistan) and abroad. These announcements are still continuing in Rojhilat. It is becoming clear that these individuals are the living realities of this movement.




The PKK brought the Kurdish people from the brink of extinction to liberation




The people do not say that these are someone else's martyrs or someone else's children. They embrace them as their own martyrs. Our martyrs embody a reality that raises awareness, organises, builds society and creates a sense of nationhood.




The democratic nation line is developing, taking shape and coming to life under the leadership of the martyrs. The reality of the martyrs is what raises consciousness, educates, organises, and instils courage and self-sacrifice.




Therefore, alongside the leadership, the reality of the martyrs represents the most vibrant and enduring expression of the values created by the PKK. It has always been this way, and it will remain so.




The leadership values created by Leader Apo and our heroic martyrs will continue to live on in Kurdish society, in the free existence of the Kurdish people and in the development of a Kurdish democratic nation. They will continue to represent these realities. Without them, it would not be possible for Kurdish identity to exist.




The PKK has promoted many values. It brought the people back to life from their deathbed. We call it a resurrection movement. It brought the dead back to life. It brought the people from a point of complete annihilation, from a state of having been reduced to nothing, towards liberation.




It brought them from the most extreme conditions of enslavement to an awareness and will for freedom, and ultimately to living freely. By overcoming the threat of annihilation under genocide in Kurdistan, it made free existence possible. It became the creator of all developments and values in the name of freedom. As Leader Apo once said, the PKK is an endless novel, a poem, a song. It will always remain so. It continues. Its organisational existence may come to an end. The Kurdish people may continue their struggle for freedom and develop their democracy through different organisational forms, strategies and political approaches. But all of this will take place on the foundations of the values created by the PKK.




At this point, it was the PKK that laid the foundations for free existence and life. It therefore became an eternal light that will never be extinguished. And it will always remain so. Undoubtedly, another hugely significant achievement of the PKK was the women's freedom revolution: the development of the women's freedom movement and struggle.




Women played a leading role in the popular uprisings (

serhildan

). The women's freedom movement provided the ideological and organisational leadership of the entire struggle. Women both took the lead and guided the movement towards what it considered the correct path. They also instilled courage and a spirit of self-sacrifice. They became the guarantee of victory and the creators of success.




They brought about the emergence of a Kurdish society liberated along the lines of women's freedom. They challenged and broke the male backwardness, domination and individualism that had persisted throughout history. The struggle continues on this basis today.




27 November marks the 48th anniversary of the PKK's founding. 25 November, meanwhile, is the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women. It is an important and deeply meaningful day, one directly connected to the founding of the PKK. The PKK challenged and broke patriarchal mentality, systems, emotions and ways of thinking. On the basis of women's freedom, it brought about the rebirth and development of both women and men.




This was not merely a struggle against violence. It genuinely enabled the strongest development and realisation of a freedom revolution. It transformed the struggle against violence towards women into a women's freedom revolution. It elevated it to the level of a women's freedom revolution that leads all democratic and social revolutions. This, too, is an extremely important value.




Today, women everywhere are making statements and raising their voices on 25 November to protest patriarchal male violence and to proclaim their demands for an independent stance and a free life. I salute all these efforts and struggles. I truly believe that these occasions should prompt a much deeper examination of patriarchal mentality.




I also call on all men to distance themselves from violence — particularly violence against women — which is the starting point of their own enslavement, and to critically examine their own attitudes and behaviour.

title: Families of seriously ill prisoners launch vigil in Ankara
content:
Families of seriously ill political prisoners began an indefinite sit-in outside the Turkish Ministry of Justice in Ankara on Tuesday. Together with members of parliament from the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) and human rights organizations, they are demanding the release of ill prisoners and access to adequate medical treatment. The participants announced that they would continue their protest until concrete steps are taken.




The vigil was organized at the call of DEM Party MPs, the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), and the Human Rights Association (IHD). Among the participants are relatives of Newroz Bozkurt, who was transferred from Sincan Women’s Prison to Etlik City Hospital, and Evin Zapsu, who is imprisoned in Kayseri Bünyan Women’s Prison with stage four cancer.




The demonstrators unfurled a banner bearing the names of seriously ill prisoners and the words: “We stand at the gates of justice. Through resistance, we will open the prison gates – Freedom for sick prisoners.” Slogans demanding the release of political prisoners were repeatedly chanted.




“People must no longer die in prisons”




Şirin Altay, the Ankara representative of the Federation of Solidarity Associations for Prisoners’ Families (TUHAD-FED), stated that the situation of seriously ill prisoners had not changed despite numerous protests and public appeals outside the Ministry of Justice. For this reason, the families have decided to launch an indefinite protest, Altay said and called on the authorities to facilitate the immediate release of prisoners and thereby strengthen public confidence in the ongoing peace process.













“People must no longer die in prisons. They must be able to receive medical treatment under appropriate conditions. The Ministry of Justice must hear our voices,” Altay said. She questioned the authorities’ responsibility for the deaths of political prisoners and demanded an answer as to how a peace process could move forward while people continued to die in detention. She stressed that the families would remain outside the ministry to fight for the lives of their loved ones.




“We cannot bear any more news of deaths”




DEM Party MP Ali Bozan recalled political prisoner Tuncer Sağlam, who recently died. He remarked that the continued refusal to release prisoners and provide adequate medical care was not only a human rights issue but also placed a burden on the social peace process. “We cannot bear any more news of deaths from prisons,” Bozan stated. Pointing out that the public was right to question how peace could be discussed while seriously ill people continued to be held in prison, he stated: "The vigil is therefore also intended to contribute to the peace process by drawing attention to the urgently needed humanitarian measures. Where rights violations continue indefinitely, protests will also continue indefinitely."




Mother of Newroz Bozkurt demands treatment outside prison




Sultan Bozkurt gave a particularly moving account of her daughter Newroz’s situation. She said her daughter had been seriously ill for a year. "Although she is now in hospital, she remains under prison conditions. When this process began two years ago, we hoped that we might be able to embrace our children again in good health,” she stated.




Sultan Bozkurt said she had traveled from Istanbul to Ankara and had been allowed to see her daughter for only ten minutes over the course of two days. "My daughter's health has deteriorated significantly. She is in a terrible condition. Her blood levels have dropped to zero,” Bozkurt said. She demanded that her daughter be transferred to a regular hospital ward and receive treatment under appropriate conditions.




She emphasized that no new law was needed to ensure medical care and the release of seriously ill prisoners. "Those affected must be given the opportunity to continue their treatment outside prison and in a family environment. We said that mothers would no longer have to cry when there is peace. We will do everything in our power to ensure that mothers no longer cry. Tears have no color. Now, concrete steps must finally be taken.”













Evin Zapsu can barely manage her daily life




Mecit Zapsu, the husband of seriously ill prisoner Evin Zapsu, also appealed to the Ministry of Justice. He criticized the apparent treatment of medical care for prisoners as a concession, even though it was a fundamental right. He said his wife is suffering from stage four cancer in Kayseri-Bünyan Prison, with her health deteriorating steadily. According to Mecit Zapsu, attempts are being made to manage her symptoms with painkillers rather than ensuring adequate medical care.




"Evin Zapsu is now unable to meet her daily needs independently. “We are here to remind the Ministry of Justice of its responsibility. The denial of adequate medical treatment worsens the prisoners’ conditions and endangers their lives. Our protest will continue until the prisoners receive treatment and are released," Mecit Zapsu stated..

title: Numerous politicians detained in operation against Kurdish party alliance Hevbendî in Turkey
content:
Numerous Kurdish politicians have been detained in Turkey as part of a large-scale operation targeting the newly formed party alliance Hevbendî. Among those detained is Bayram Bozyel, chairman of the Socialist Party of Kurdistan (PSK). The public prosecutor’s office in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) accuses members of the alliance of endangering the unity of the state and Turkey’s territorial integrity. According to Hevbendî, the investigation covers all 51 members of the alliance’s council.




Hevbendî was founded on November 7 in Amed as the “National Alliance of Kurdistan.” Its members include the PSK, the Kurdistan Democratic Party/North (PDK-Bakur), the Patriotic Party of Kurdistan (PWK), Pêlkurd, Vejîn, and the Kurdistan National Initiative. The alliance aims to strengthen cooperation among Kurdish parties and political movements.




House raids in five cities




Police raided homes in Amed, Ankara, Mardin, Batman, and Istanbul in the early hours of November 17. According to Hevbendî, those detained included Bayram Bozyel, PSK deputy chairman and lawyer Hasan Dağtekin, Pêlkurd spokesperson Fuat Önen, PWK deputy chairman Mehmet Can Azbay, as well as Sevgi Çelik, Aryan Serhed, Ali Öncü, Rojbin Bükün, Ali Çeven, and Ali Aydın.




The home of PWK chairman Mustafa Özçelik was also raided and searched. According to the alliance, an arrest warrant has also been issued for him. Those targeted are accused under Article 302 of the Turkish Penal Code of “disrupting the unity of the state and the territorial integrity of the country.” The offense carries a sentence of aggravated life imprisonment. According to the alliance, the investigation files have been placed under a confidentiality order, and those detained have been denied access to their lawyers for 24 hours.




PSK: “This repression will not intimidate us”




The PSK condemned the detentions and announced that it would continue its political activities. “These and similar repressive measures, as well as the detention of our officials, will not intimidate us. We will continue to struggle alongside all patriotic forces until the Kurdish people achieve their national and democratic rights,” the party stated. It also called on democratic organizations and the public to oppose the measures and show solidarity with Hevbendî. “We will not be intimidated and will continue to stand up for Hevbendî.”




Solidarity appeal criticizes criminalization of peaceful political activity




In a joint appeal titled “Shoulder to Shoulder: Solidarity with the Hevbendî Detainees,” intellectuals, writers, academics, and artists condemned the operation. They pointed out that the accusations concerned a political conference, a joint program, and a press conference, none of which had involved acts of violence or calls for violence.




The signatories described the detentions as a violation of freedom of expression and association under the Turkish Constitution and the European Convention on Human Rights. They also referred to the case law of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR), according to which peaceful advocacy for the right to self-determination was not in itself a criminal offense.




‘Those who expected division have strengthened unity’




The signatories stated that the repression had fostered solidarity among different Kurdish political movements, some of which had previously had significant differences. “The national unity that the Kurdish people were unable to achieve through their own efforts over the years has now emerged on its own as a result of a single arrest warrant. People of different views and traditions who long kept their distance from one another are now signing the same declaration.”




They emphasized, however, that their previous objections to the establishment, working methods, and structures of Hevbendî remained unchanged. In light of the detentions, however, solidarity with those affected took precedence. “We will conduct our discussions on procedural matters among ourselves and on our own terms, just as a family discusses its affairs within the family. We will not allow these debates to become material for prosecutors’ investigation files or indictments.”




Alliance for national rights and political self-determination




Hevbendî emerged from a prolonged process of political rapprochement. The starting point was a conference on Kurdistan’s national unity held in Amed on March 14, 2026. At another conference on November 7, a joint program was adopted, before the alliance was publicly introduced on November 9.




In its founding declaration, Hevbendî calls for recognition of the collective rights of the Kurdish people, the right to self-determination, and political status for Kurdistan. Its objectives also include constitutional recognition of Kurdish identity, the use of Kurdish as an official language and a language of education, and stronger cooperation among Kurdish political forces in all four parts of Kurdistan.




The alliance elected a 51-member council to coordinate joint political activities. Following its establishment, PSK chairman Bayram Bozyel stated that political status for the Kurds could be achieved within Turkey’s existing borders, for example through a federal system or another model.

title: Rojhilat Alliance: Tehran is the source of all crises and threats to people’s lives and security
content:
The Alliance of Iranian Kurdistan Political Parties issued a statement regarding the protests organized by the people of Awdanan in Eastern Kurdistan against the deaths of workers caused by poor road conditions, and the harsh intervention of regime forces.




The statement on Wednesday said: “These tragic deaths of workers have once again exposed the inadequacy of emergency services, poor road conditions, and the irresponsibility of the relevant institutions. This has sparked a wave of anger among the people of Awdanan. However, yesterday’s protests in Awdanan were not limited to demanding accountability from those responsible for the deaths of the workers but quickly took on a political character directed against the government.




Kurds across the country have once again seen that Tehran is the source of all crises and threats to their lives and security. At the same time, they have come to understand that there is no prospect for reform within this regime or of an end to the turmoil, crises, and suffering. As a result, the voices raised against poor conditions and corrupt officials quickly turned into a united protest against the entire regime.”

title: Kalkan: Those obstructing release of prisoners oppose the Peace and Democratic Society Process
content:
Duran Kalkan, a member of the Abdullah Öcalan Academy of Social Sciences, gave a lengthy interview to Medya Haber TV.




In the second part of this lengthy interview, he spoke about the need for the government to move on prisoners, the ecology and the recurrent deaths in the workplace. 




Part one of the interview can be read 

here

. 




Ecology is also one of the pillars of your paradigm. You have been regularly discussing the ecological struggle in your programmes for some time. Ecology was particularly prominent on the agenda this week, especially because of COP31 held in Antalya. Firstly, how do you view and assess such summits? There have been strong reactions against them. Alternative summits and forums are now being organised by the peoples. How should we approach and evaluate these emerging movements?




People want to be hopeful. They want to see value in what is being done. Such gatherings were also held in the past. There were discussions of this kind when the Soviet Union existed. We were not very aware of these issues at the time, and I do not have a complete understanding of them either. I do not want to make a mistake, but it seems to me that things were taken more seriously back then. Now that seriousness has disappeared. They talk and hold discussions in Antalya. They call it the COP31 summit, the climate summit. I listened to some of the speeches. There are also accurate assessments. But what happens? The necessary measures arising from those assessments are not implemented. Some say there is hypocrisy. That is true. I agree with that. Those organising COP31 are the ones responsible for this situation. We could even call them the culprits. They are the ones destroying the climate. Of course, one might say that they have caused damage, committed crimes and made mistakes, and that they are now gathering to discuss these issues, cooperate with one another and resolve the situation. If that were the case, it would be good. But that is not what happens. They keep holding these meetings, while the existing situation continues to worsen and deepen. Climate deterioration continues to increase.




As a result of the capitalist system's greed for exploitation and profit, there is an endless assault on society and nature. Never before have nature and society been endangered to the extent they are today. Human activity has brought them to this point. What is called the crisis of capitalism today is precisely the level reached by the system of capitalist modernity. It is something resembling a sign of the apocalypse. That is the extent of the situation. Those responsible can also see what is happening. They should engage in self-criticism and correct their mistakes. They should take some corrective steps and introduce at least partial restrictions. But nothing is being done. They keep talking as though they are confessing their sins, and then they return to their old practices. It becomes a form of deception. Nobody should be deceived. We will not allow ourselves to be deceived by this situation. If they are genuinely sincere, they can immediately take decisions and implement appropriate measures. Industry does not have to operate in this way. Nobody should claim that this is an inevitable consequence of industrial development. Industry can be used for the benefit of the peoples. Production can be planned and organised according to needs, according to the needs of humanity. Nobody would die of hunger, go hungry or fall into poverty.




But when industry is driven by the desire of certain people to destroy nature and other sections of society, seize everything and accumulate enormous wealth for themselves, it becomes the most dangerous instrument. That is what it has become in their hands. They have transformed it into such an instrument and are continuing this process in competition with one another. Their rivalry and conflicts are entirely shaped by this. These realities must be recognised. In this sense, the initiatives organised under the names of alternative climate summits and peoples' climate summits are important. The discussions are important. People are struggling, and I find these efforts important and meaningful. I salute the struggle to protect our home, the place where we live, against this hypocrisy and the assault on nature. I regard it as a legitimate struggle. But it must go further. It must genuinely produce alternatives. We must create alternatives. We should not be satisfied merely with verbally criticising and condemning what already exists. We should not simply protest when they gather and then go home. We must struggle at every moment of practical life.




'They are destroying people's living spaces for a handful of wealth'




The people of the Black Sea region, for example, have resisted the plunder and destruction of nature carried out under the Justice and Development Party (AKP). The people of Kurdistan are also resisting. Kurdistan has been subjected to outright ecocide, plunder and destruction. Forests have been destroyed, land continues to be taken, and water resources and mountains have not been spared. They are on the verge of destroying entire mountains. They are destroying people's living spaces simply to create a handful of sources of wealth. That is how dangerous the situation has become. We must struggle against these practices in every sphere. The ecological struggle is one of the most fundamental struggles for freedom and democracy, advancing alongside and in parallel with the struggle for women's freedom. One pillar of today's democratic struggle is women's freedom, and the other is social ecology. The struggle for a democratic society comes out of these foundations.




The democratic communal movement develops on these foundations. This is how a level of development emerges in which society governs itself and regains its moral and political values. They have even chosen a place like Antalya for this summit. In a sense, it almost seems as though they are mocking people. It is an insult to humanity. Everyone must take these matters seriously. There must be some respect. Human life has meaning. Nature has meaning. All living beings have meaning. This is not something exclusive to human beings. What is being done does not destroy only human beings; it destroys all living beings. We must show some respect for life. Any being that has no respect for life has no meaning. That is the point we have reached. Therefore, ecological consciousness, ecological organisation and ecological struggle must always exist. They must not emerge only when a climate summit such as COP31 is convened. Wherever and whenever the assault known as industrialism takes place, there must be alternative organisation and resistance against it. The possibility of living freely and democratically, of existing with human dignity, depends on carrying out such a struggle and achieving results.




You mentioned living with human dignity. Prisons are another area where life is under attack. Tuncer Sağlam lost his life. I believe you said in your previous programme that if someone died or was martyred in prison, you would consider them a martyr of the war. Now such an incident has occurred.




Yes, I commemorate Tuncer Sağlam with respect and gratitude. He is a martyr of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, our martyr of peace and democracy. Over the past year and a half, there have been more such martyrs coming out of prisons. This shows that the struggle continues with the same intensity in one area. If the fighting in the mountains has stopped, it is because we stopped it. I can say that clearly. But we cannot stop what is happening in the prisons. That is not in our hands. It is clear who controls the situation in prisons and who has the power to change it. The government and the state bear responsibility. It used to be said that the state is responsible for everyone who enters prison. Prisoners are subjected to the most severe torture and insults. They complete the sentences imposed under existing laws, yet they are still not released. They become ill, they are denied treatment, and their bodies are brought out of prison. This shows that the state is at war with prisoners.




We know that there are hundreds of prisoners who have completed 30 years in prison. Some have been imprisoned for 33 or 35 years. What do they say? "They have not abandoned their beliefs." Those boards that refuse to release them are actually opposed to this process. Because when prisoners are released, they declare at the prison gates their commitment to the Peace and Democratic Society Process and their intention to struggle in accordance with its requirements. Those who are not released are being kept in prison precisely to prevent them from participating in the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Therefore, those obstructing their release are opposed to the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Apparently, there are also vested interests within the legal system. We have said that there are groups benefiting from the existing system and opponents of the process. A stratum opposed to the process has been created within the justice system and the legal sphere. Or perhaps they are using that sphere to carry out what they want to achieve elsewhere, assigning it this responsibility. Last time, we said that there was an outright hostage system. Yes, being held hostage means being forcibly detained. These people are being forcibly held, and every form of coercion is being used against them. That coercion continues until they lose their lives. This is the level at which the struggle continues.




As long as prisons remain in this condition and bodies continue to emerge from them, nobody should expect peace or democracy to arrive. How could that happen? So many prisoners' families and Peace Mothers are holding rallies and making statements, saying that this situation cannot continue. Yet it continues. This is also a measure of how the current government and the AKP approach the Peace and Democratic Society Process. They cannot say, "We have no power, we cannot intervene." The Minister of Justice is responsible for the administration of these institutions. The minister can take whatever decisions are necessary. The government is in charge. Therefore, when such an obvious reality exists, can there be any credibility in claims that " leaders of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) are obstructing the process" or similar accusations? Who would believe such statements? Nobody has believed them anyway. It is clear who is obstructing the process and who opposes it. The situation is therefore extremely serious.




Acts of solidarity with prisoners are very important and meaningful. I salute all of them. The struggle carried out by mothers is particularly valuable and meaningful. Everyone should participate. This struggle must grow. In fact, when that body was brought out of prison, millions of people should have gathered at the gates. They should have protested. The government would then have been unable to continue as before. It would have been forced to make changes and open the way for democratic conduct and attitudes. This can only happen through struggle. Nobody gives anything to anyone voluntarily. Rights can only be won through struggle. It has been said that "Rights are not given, they are won." This is the most general principle. We must therefore fulfil its requirements. Once again, I commemorate Tuncer Sağlam with respect and gratitude. He is a martyr of the struggle, and one day those responsible will be held to account.




Following this killing, news emerged almost immediately of the killing of 19 workers at the Izmir plant of HABAŞ, a Turkish iron and steel manufacturer. Dozens of others were also injured. How do you assess the emergence of such incidents at a time when discussions related to the process are continuing?




What can I say? We are discussing the process and what it requires. On one side, there is the climate summit in Antalya. On another, bodies are being brought out of prisons, where so much torture and repression continue. Elsewhere, people are being arrested. We are told that the age of drug use has fallen to five. Drugs and prostitution are being systematically and deliberately spread throughout the cities of Kurdistan, and special warfare policies are being escalated to their highest level. Women are being killed everywhere. Every day, several such reports appear in the media. It almost seems as though seeing these incidents encourages others. All of this actually reveals the nature of the current administration. The killing of workers is another consequence of this. There was the fund crisis. So much money was stolen and embezzled. People said, "This is only the tip of the iceberg." Much more remains concealed. It is not being exposed. But how long can this continue? This is a system of repression and exploitation. It has reached such a point that it is falling apart.




The entire system has come apart at the seams. Naturally, it is the poor who suffer. Women suffer. Children suffer. Young people suffer. Kurds suffer. Alevis suffer. The oppressed suffer. They are the ones paying the price for a system that has completely fallen apart. The workers have suffered in the same way. It is not only the killing of 19 workers in Izmir. Recently, figures were published showing how many workers had died in various places in what are described as occupational accidents. This is a serious situation, an extremely important issue. If these incidents were genuinely unavoidable, one might have nothing to say. But that is not the case. All of them are preventable. They are not accidents. They are consequences created by human actions and the desire to make ever greater profits. They have nothing to do with accidents, disasters or anything of that kind. They are massacres and murders. All of them must be treated as such. People are so poor that they are forced to work under those conditions. If they had even a little more economic security, nobody would accept such work. Therefore, trade unions, working-class movements and organisations must become more sensitive to this issue.




A more effective struggle is needed. There is talk about workers and their rights, but there is no organisation and no struggle. Everything is extremely scattered and fragmented. That is what we see. The government acts without restraint, while the owners of capital operate with virtually no accountability. The workers' movement, trade unions and political movements have become so weak. Workers are unorganised and lack awareness. We must overcome this situation. We must free ourselves from it. This requires consciousness, organisation and struggle. It is truly impossible not to feel anger. I condemn this massacre. I commemorate the workers who were killed with respect and gratitude. I share the grief of their families. But saying these things is not enough. Organisation and struggle are necessary. We must all work together, using our strength to the fullest extent, and know how to put an end to this system of massacres and plunder.

title: Activists in Strasbourg: Our vigil will continue until Abdullah Öcalan is free
content:
The Freedom for Öcalan Vigil, launched on 25 June 2012 in Strasbourg to demand the physical freedom of the Kurdish people's leader, is continuing into its 751st week.




This week, the vigil was taken over by Kadriye Alptekin, Merve Zîlan and Ömer Kurtgözü, who travelled from Brussels.




Speaking at the event, Kadriye Alptekin thanked everyone who had contributed to the action over the past 15 years, stating that they would continue their struggle until Öcalan achieved physical freedom.




“Until our Leader achieves physical freedom, we will all be here, we will all stand firm, and we will all continue to make our call,” Alptekin said.




She concluded her speech with the words: “Long live the Kurds and Kurdistan; long live Abdullah Öcalan, the leader of the people of Kurdistan.”




Merve Zîlan, another activist who took over the vigil, said they had come from Brussels and would continue their vigil and actions until Öcalan's physical freedom was secured.




Calling on European public opinion to show greater awareness, Zîlan said: “We have joined this vigil, which has been continuing for 15 years. We will continue our vigils and actions until our Leader is free and achieves physical freedom. Our appeal to Europe is to show support for our struggle for our Leader's freedom.”

title: Iraqi Court orders closure of Yazidi Youth Party
content:
The Iraqi Federal Court ruled on 13 October 2026, to dissolve the Yazidi Youth Party. An appeal against the decision was filed with the Iraqi Federal Court and accepted. However, at the request of the Political Parties Department of the Iraqi High Electoral Commission, the Court ruled on 15 November to shut down the party.




Following the 13 October closure decision by Iraq’s Electoral Legal Committee, the president of the Yazidi Youth Party appealed to the court, arguing that the decision was unjust and requesting its annulment.




The Federal Court found that the appeal had been filed within the legal deadline and accepted it on procedural grounds. However, during its review, the Court upheld the closure decision, stating that it was based on security reports submitted by security forces. According to the Court, the department’s report concluded that the party’s activities “threaten the security, territorial integrity, and sovereignty of the Republic of Iraq.”




Consequently, Decision No. 20, dated 13 October, issued by the Electoral Legal Committee, was upheld. The ruling ordered the party to cease its activities, all its offices to be closed, and its assets to be confiscated.

title: Iran attacks Pêncewîn and Qandil in Southern Kurdistan
content:
Iranian regime forces carried out several attacks on areas along the border between Southern and Eastern Kurdistan on Tuesday. In addition to mortar attacks on the Qandil region, a drone attack on Pêncewîn (Penjwen) in Sulaymaniyah Governorate was also reported in the evening.




According to a statement issued by the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), regime forces targeted several locations in the Pêncewîn region with an explosive-laden kamikaze drone at around 7:30 pm. The PJAK stated that the attack had caused no fatalities among its ranks.




Mortar shelling of villages in the Qandil region




Earlier in the day, Iranian regime forces had subjected several areas in the Qandil Mountains to mortar fire. According to information from the region, the areas of Şehîd Harûn and Şehîd Ayhan, as well as the villages of Elî Reş and Goyêz along the border between Southern and Eastern Kurdistan, were affected. No information was initially available on the extent of the damage or possible casualties from the shelling.

title: American philosopher Caputo voices support for the Peace and Democratic Society Process
content:
International solidarity continues with the Call for Peace and Democratic Society issued by Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan on February 27, 2025. American philosopher John David Caputo has also expressed his support for the international campaign being conducted as part of the call.




In a message sent to Mezopotamya Agency (MA), Caputo expressed his hopes for the ongoing peace process in Turkey in the following words:




“My hope is that the ongoing peace process in Turkey will embrace the following principles: Diversity fosters a deeper unity; a genuine community is formed by weaving bonds across differences; and true peace is the fruit of justice.”




John David Caputo




Born in 1940, John David Caputo is an American philosopher and philosopher of religion. One of the prominent figures in contemporary continental philosophy, Caputo is particularly known for his work on Jacques Derrida’s deconstruction, hermeneutics, and radical theology.




A leading representative of radical hermeneutics and “weak theology,” Caputo has served as a professor at Villanova University and Syracuse University.




His major works include 

Radical Hermeneutics

 (1987), 

The Weakness of God: A Theology of the Event

 (2006), and 

The Insistence of God: A Theology of Perhaps

 (2013).

author: Unknown
title: Karayılan: The PKK created a national spirit and consciousness
content:
Murat Karayılan, Commander of the People's Defence Centre (HSM), talked to Egîd Sîrwan on Stêrk TV about the ongoing political process.




In the second part of the interview, he spoke about the importance of the PKK in bringing the Kurdish people "back from the brink of extinction." Talking about the upcoming 25 November, he said that "talking about creating a free society without liberating women is an empty claim with no foundation."




The first part of the interview can be read 

here

. 




The PKK fought for Kurdish freedom for half a century. What impact did it have on the struggle for freedom, not only in Kurdistan but throughout the region? In short, what has the PKK achieved over these 48 years?




The Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) brought the Kurdish people back from the brink of extinction, helped them rise to their feet and brought them to the negotiating table. That is what it achieved, to put it very briefly. But if we elaborate, we can assess this from several perspectives.




At the national level, 48 years of resistance put an end to the genocide carried out in Kurdistan under the Eastern Reform Plan (Şark Islahat Planı), the Turkish state's historical policy of assimilation and repression. In doing so, it guaranteed the existence of the Kurdish people and brought their existence onto the agenda in a way that nobody could deny.




At the social level, this resistance developed like a renaissance in Kurdistan. It overcame centuries of backwardness. At the intellectual level, there was almost a revolution in thought. A complete transformation took place, bringing about a profound renewal of society. It developed a social revolution. It transformed a people who had given up on themselves and lost hope into a people who had risen to their feet, regained hope and begun to struggle, carrying forward the struggle for freedom and democracy of our age. It reached that level.




At the same time, it developed the Women's Revolution in Kurdistan. Through the struggle against the male-dominated mentality and efforts to transform that mentality, it enabled women to develop their own will and agency. It laid the foundations for such profound social transformations.




'The PKK guaranteed the existence of the Kurdish people'




At the political level, it brought the Kurdish question to the negotiating table. Through struggle, resistance and different methods, it created Kurdish politics. Previously, Kurds fought only in the mountains. The political sphere had effectively been left to the colonial powers. The movement developed a tradition of conducting politics on the political ground established by the state itself. This struggle also has its martyrs and prisoners. Important developments have been achieved in this field as well.




'The PKK created a national spirit and consciousness'




This struggle influenced all four parts of Kurdistan. It created a national spirit and consciousness. Previously, the different parts of Kurdistan were distant from one another, separated by borders. The struggle rendered those borders meaningless. A young person from Lorestan turned their attention towards another part of Kurdistan, towards Dersim. Young people from Kermanshah and Ardalan turned their attention towards all of Kurdistan. The same happened in Qamishlo, Kobanê, Amed (Diyarbakır), Erbil (Hewlêr) and Sulaymaniyah (Silêmanî). In short, people from every part participated. This attracted the attention of many people. It was, in particular, a movement of intellectuals. It always had an influence among university students. Through its cadres, it created a national spirit and consciousness at that level.




It also achieved very important developments at the internationalist level. As is known, internationalism has been part of this movement from its very foundation. Comrades Haki and Kemal were among its founders. These ideas became known throughout the world. Today, there are many Arab and Turkish cadres, as well as cadres from numerous other peoples. In other words, it became a universal idea. A foundation for internationalist work has now emerged. This, too, represents an achievement.




During the period when the PKK was carrying out its struggle, actually existing socialism collapsed. It appeared as though humanity had become condemned to capitalism. However, the struggle that was carried out, together with the theoretical depth developed by Leader Apo (Abdullah Öcalan), both before and after his imprisonment on Imrali Island, sent a message to the world: "No, we are not condemned to capitalist modernity. We have an alternative. It is true that nation-state socialism collapsed, but there is democratic society socialism. It can bring victory and show the way forward." He developed Democratic Modernity, a democratic and ecological paradigm based on women's freedom, as an alternative to capitalist modernity. As these ideas spread around the world, they generated influence and hope.




This movement also achieved major developments through resistance. The emergence of ISIS (Islamic State of Iraq and Syria) created a grave danger. However, the interventions in Shengal and Kobanê, and the resistance extending from Kirkuk to Afrin (Efrîn), effectively formed a barrier against the ISIS threat. The Rojava Revolution developed as a result of this historic resistance. Most importantly, never before in Kurdish history had there been a struggle in which fighters held the same positions for five years, resisted and remained undefeated. With NATO's support, the Turkish state attempted to destroy us not once but dozens of times. The International Conspiracy was carried out. An unprecedented resistance developed. At the point we have reached today, revolution is on the agenda not only in one country but throughout the region, together with change and transformation. In particular, the new initiative developed by Leader Apo, the initiative for peace, democratic society and democratic integration, has opened the way for major developments throughout the region.




'

People rallied around the Apoist movement because its words matched its actions'




None of this was easy, of course. These achievements were the result of the efforts of many heroes. Beginning with Leader Apo, all members of this movement remained faithful to their words. Whatever promises they made to their society, they put them into practice. They worked towards fulfilling those promises. They did not betray their dreams. That is how they proceeded. People rallied around the movement because they saw that its words and actions were consistent. There were many other organisations before us. Why did they fall behind and become marginalised? Some explain this in various ways, but the truth is that the Apoist members of this movement, formerly known as PKK members, put whatever they said into practice. They did so even at the cost of their lives. The courage of women and men became evident. That is why the people rallied around this movement, and they will continue to do so. Because the struggle continues. In the new period, with a new strategy, the Apoist Movement will grow and develop even further.




'Everyone, from the founders to the commanders, fought with self-sacrifice'




Comrades Haki Karer, Mazlum Doğan, Mehmet Hayri Durmuş, Kemal Pir, Ferhat Kurtay and Mehmet Karasungur, as well as Heval Fuat (Ali Haydar Kaytan), Rıza Altun, Sara (Sakine Cansız) and Seyfi Zoğurlu, who carried out a long period of practical struggle, and many other comrades were founders of this movement, yet they gave their lives in the course of the struggle. At the level of the general guerrilla command, from comrade Egîd to the Erdals, Bedrans, Azimes, Zelals and Zîlans; following the 1 June Initiative, the Adıls, Nudas, Reşits and Rojîns; and, more recently, comrades Nurettîn Sofî, Atakan Mahir, Delal Amed, Leyla Amed and Gulçiya Gabar, who served in the general command and were among those leading this movement; as well as comrades Sabri Tendürek, Egîd Civyan, Şivan Gever, Azad Sîser, Doğan Didêrî, Berçem Cîlo, Yılmaz Dersîm, Çetin Siverek, Zinê Cizre, Şêxmus Malazgirt, Berwar Dersîm and Axîn Mûş, all led this movement and were at the forefront when they fell as martyrs. In the recent tunnel resistance, comrades Nurî Yekta, Azê Şirnex, Alan Malazgirt, Siyabend, Mizgîn Ronahî, Cumali and Çavrê, Delil Zagros, Mordem Çewlig and Sarya Qamışlo, along with many other comrades serving in regional and provincial commands, all stood at the forefront, gave their lives and attained martyrdom.




'We lost 50,000 martyrs in 48 years of struggle'




Taken as a whole, the Apoist Movement has lost approximately 50,000 martyrs across all four parts of Kurdistan, including leaders, guerrillas, fighters, militia members, supporters, workers and civilians, because, as is known, resistance along this political line was also carried out in the other parts of Kurdistan. So many martyrs were lost over these 48 years, and these developments were achieved through their sacrifices. Today, as a result of these developments, our people can look towards the future with their heads held high and have reached a level where they can achieve their goals.




25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, is approaching. Violence against women remains extremely widespread in society. How effective is the struggle against violence against women worldwide? How do you assess it?




A struggle against violence against women is being carried out today. Firstly, I salute everyone involved in this struggle. This is also our struggle as a movement. What is the source of violence against women? It is male domination. The male-dominated mentality is the source of violence against women. We want to eliminate male domination. As a movement, we are carrying out a profound struggle to transform this mentality. Because women must be liberated for society to become free.




'We want to achieve a free society by creating free women and men'




Talking about creating a free society without liberating women is an empty claim with no foundation. If you genuinely want to create a free society, the sexes must first be liberated. Women must be liberated. For women, and therefore society, to become free, the male-dominated mentality must be eliminated. This is necessary not only for women's freedom but also for the freedom of society. That is why we pursue a much more fundamental struggle. If this struggle advances and achieves results, the source of violence against women will also be eliminated, and the foundations of a free society will be established. If women become free in a society, and men can free themselves from the hollow mentality of domination, men will also become free. That is our aim. We want to achieve a free society by creating free women and free men. This is extremely important, historic and sacred. That is why everyone struggling against violence against women is valuable, and we fully support this struggle. We also want to integrate this struggle much more fundamentally into our revolutionary struggle and genuinely turn a free society into a reality. Of course, on this basis, we also say, "Jin, Jiyan, Azadî" (Woman, Life, Freedom).




Recently the Press Liaison Centre of the People's Defense Forces (HPG) announced commemorations of martyrs from Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilat). We see this as an expression of the spirit of national unity among the different parts of Kurdistan. You had issued a message to the families of the martyrs. What can you say about the participation of young people from Eastern Kurdistan? Everyone is also wondering where the situation in Eastern Kurdistan is heading and what will happen.




Firstly, I would like to take this opportunity to greet our valued people of Eastern Kurdistan with respect and affection. We have recently announced the names of some of our martyrs. We will announce the remaining names within the next ten days. I commemorate all these martyrs with respect and gratitude. I bow respectfully before their memory. They are the heroes of this era. All our valued families should know that the daughters and sons they raised played an important role for the Kurdish people and attained martyrdom. So far, we have announced the martyrs from certain regions. The martyrs from Urmia will be announced today or tomorrow. Then approximately 40 comrades from Salmas, Khoy (Xoy), Kotol, Marivan (Merîwan) and the Kalhor region will remain. We will announce those comrades within the next ten days as well.




'The martyrs have paved the way for national unity'




They are national heroes. They set out from places as far away as Kalhor or Ardalan, travelled to Northern Kurdistan (Bakur) and Southern Kurdistan (Başûr), and joined the national struggle. What could be more valuable and honourable than that? The young women and men of the Kurdish people regard this as their responsibility. They leave their own regions and travel to another part of Kurdistan to struggle for a united and free Kurdistan. They fight wholeheartedly for years and attain martyrdom. This is a sign of the Kurdish people's victory. This is the path towards Kurdish national unity. Someone from Lorestan, Kalhor or Ilam turns towards Northern Kurdistan. This is no ordinary matter. Moreover, these are not children. Many of them attended university. They studied, came to believe in Leader Apo's ideas and, on that basis, decided to become militants, fighters and commanders of this people. Indeed, many of them reached that level.




'They did everything they could to destroy us'




There is another matter that all our people in Eastern Kurdistan should know. I believe many of them are already following these developments and are aware of them. Particularly over the past ten years, we have faced extremely severe attacks. As you know, our Yazidi (Êzidî) people use the word "ferman" to describe campaigns of genocide and extermination. It refers to a ruler issuing a decree of extermination, bringing catastrophe upon a people. Over the past ten years, the Turkish state has effectively declared such a campaign of destruction against us. To destroy us as a movement, it obtained support from NATO, acquired modern weapons, reorganised the state internally and concentrated all power in a single authority. It sought to destroy us through attacks using the most advanced weapons of our time. Twice, they set deadlines for our destruction. First, they said the PKK would be finished by April 2017. April 2017 came and went, but the PKK was not defeated. Then, in 2021, they developed another plan and launched an attack on Garê. At that time, they formed alliances with various forces, including Iraq, and gave themselves three months to finish us. To destroy us, they used prohibited chemical weapons, tactical nuclear weapons and every kind of modern weapon against us. But an historic resistance developed against them.




'I respectfully salute the families of the martyrs'




Never in the history of our people's struggle has there been such prolonged resistance in the same position. For example, there was the resistance of Kela Dimdimê, which is said to have lasted more than a year. But the resistance in Zap lasted five years. For five years, resistance was maintained in the same positions against these powerful and prohibited weapons. There is intelligence, willpower and determination behind this resistance. This is not something ordinary people could accomplish. The heroes whose names we have announced were participants in this resistance. That is why I bow before their heroism with the deepest respect. They are extremely valuable people, the heroes of this people and this era. They are truly the pioneers of our revolution. If we are here today, if we can speak in this way, if the Turkish state was forced to approach Leader Apo, and if this process has begun in Northern Kurdistan, it is thanks to these heroes. Our people in Eastern Kurdistan should understand this very well. These comrades, their own daughters and sons, created epic resistance along a historic path and attained martyrdom. For us, they are immortal. Their memory will illuminate our path, and their cause will achieve victory. Our families should approach them in this spirit and uphold the political line and cause of the martyrs. Once again, I commemorate those heroes with respect. I respectfully salute all the families of the martyrs, particularly the mothers, and offer my condolences. Our hearts have also been deeply wounded. They were our comrades. I offer my condolences to you and to all the people of Eastern Kurdistan.




'My condolences to the PJAK comrades and the people of Eastern Kurdistan'




The entire region is going through a period of great uncertainty. I believe the same is true of Eastern Kurdistan. Before addressing this issue, I would like to mention something. A statement was released to the press yesterday. Comrade Dersîm Bihar, a member of the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), has been martyred. I commemorate this valued martyr with respect and offer my condolences to the family of comrade Dersîm Bihar, all PJAK comrades and the people of Eastern Kurdistan. According to the statement, comrade Dersîm resisted and used their own weapon against themselves rather than surrender. This represents an extremely valuable, self-sacrificing and sacred spirit.




'Developments in the region will affect Eastern Kurdistan'




Our people in Eastern Kurdistan have maintained a particular position until now. This is a very meaningful position. They have not become anyone's instrument. That is extremely important. Our people should pursue a third way, avoid aligning themselves with either side and remain independent. This has been their position so far. All the organisations, including PJAK, have followed this line. We consider it appropriate. The region is going through an extremely important and uncertain period. Developments in the region will undoubtedly affect Eastern Kurdistan as well. Our people must be prepared for every possibility during this period, because anything could happen. That is why they must be ready for every eventuality. They must rely on their own strength and their own organisations. They must organise themselves, help one another as a society and strengthen solidarity. Nobody should feel alone. Society as a whole must remain united, protect one another everywhere and remain vigilant during this important period.




'The Iranian state must not regard Kurds as enemies'




What matters is doing the right thing at the right time. Doing the right thing at the wrong time can lead to mistakes. The right actions must be taken at the right time. That is why our people and their political representatives must be extremely attentive to this issue. We are optimistic about the future of Eastern Kurdistan. We believe that the developments ahead will be positive for our people. But everyone must remain calm and approach the situation with restraint. Politics, rather than war, must be the priority. The Iranian state must not attack the Kurds during this critical period or regard them as enemies. For example, when the Iranian state was at its weakest, the Kurds did nothing to harm it. This should be taken into consideration. The Kurds must also remain calm, follow developments and act accordingly. They should prioritise dialogue rather than methods based on violence. They must create a spirit of unity among themselves and with all the peoples of Iran. That would be the best approach. I believe that the future of our people in Eastern Kurdistan will be positive and successful. On this basis, I once again respectfully greet our people in Eastern Kurdistan and wish everyone success.
