author: Unknown
title: Kurdish political prisoner in Iran denied urgent treatment
content:
The Tehran Prosecutor’s Office continues to block Kurdish political prisoner Motalleb Ahmadian’s transfer outside Evin Prison for urgent medical treatment, despite repeated medical warnings over his deteriorating health and serious complications from a cancerous tumour.




Ahmadian, from Baneh, Kurdistan Province, is in his 17th year of imprisonment and suffers from multiple illnesses.




An informed source told the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN): “The Legal Medicine Organisation has repeatedly informed the judge overseeing the prison and the Tehran Prosecutor’s Office that, given the deterioration in Motalleb Ahmadian’s health, he must be transferred outside prison as soon as possible so that he can receive treatment for his multiple illnesses, undergo the necessary medical procedures and recover in suitable conditions.”




The source said the prosecutor’s office had nevertheless refused to approve the transfer, heightening concerns about irreversible harm to Ahmadian’s health and the risk to his life.




Ahmadian has undergone several operations to treat complications caused by the cancerous tumour. During these procedures, his gallbladder was completely emptied, and surgeons also operated on parts of his liver and intestines, the source said.

author: Unknown
title: Women’s movements and organizations in Rojava launch November 25 campaign
content:
The Joint Action Platform of Women’s Movements and Organizations in Rojava issued a statement at the March 12 Martyrs Stadium in Qamishlo to mark November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.




The statement, read in Kurdish, Arabic, and Syriac, announced the launch of a campaign against violence against women under the slogan “Unite: Jin, Jiyan, Azadî.”




The key points highlighted by the platform are as follows:




The scope of violence:

 The statement emphasized that violence against women is not limited to physical or psychological attacks but also encompasses deeper forms of oppression, including economic restrictions, exclusion from public life, and political and institutional marginalization.




The situation of women in Syria:

 the platform noted that women had shouldered immense burdens during years of war and crisis, playing a fundamental role in protecting society and sustaining everyday life. Nevertheless, it added, they continued to face marginalization and exclusion from decision-making mechanisms.




Warning regarding the integration process:

 The platform warned that women’s achievements to date could be undermined if potential integration or restructuring processes in Syria proceeded without adequate legal safeguards.

title: Four Kurdish citizens remain detained in Iran, whereabouts unknown
content:
Four Kurdish citizens arrested by security forces in Bukan, Miandoab and Piranshahr in West Azerbaijan Province between 2 and 4 November remain detained with their exact whereabouts and condition unknown.




The detainees – Diyar Abroun, Jamileh (Mina) Mohammadamin-Azar, Saadi Karimi, and Mahmoud Pileh – have been denied access to legal counsel and family visits since their arrests.




The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has learned that security forces violently arrested Abroun, from Piranshahr, on 2 November.




On 3 November, Ministry of Intelligence forces raided Mohammadamin-Azar’s family home in Bukan and arrested her and her husband, Khoshnaw Azizpour, without a warrant.




Azizpour was released after several hours of interrogation, while Mohammadamin-Azar was reportedly transferred to a security detention facility in Orumiyeh, the provincial capital, with her exact place of detention remaining unknown.




Security forces also arrested Karimi, another citizen from Bukan, on the same day.




On 4 November, security forces arrested Pileh, from the village of Gug Jalu in Miandoab County.

title: Yıldız Çakar’s poetry wins international award in the US
content:
The poem “Mohra Reş” (The Dark Seal) by Kurdish poet and novelist Yıldız Çakar has won the Special International Honorable Mention at the Julia Vive Feminist Poetry Festival, held in Philadelphia, USA. The award, presented in the category of “Poetry, Memory and Resistance,” recognizes Çakar’s distinctive literary treatment of women’s struggle, collective memory and resistance.




Organized by the Madre Tierra Women’s Center (CIMMT), the Julia Vive Feminist Poetry Festival will take place on November 13 at the Taller Puertorriqueño Cultural Center in Philadelphia. Bringing together 100 poets from different parts of the world, the festival selected Yıldız Çakar’s poem “Mohra Reş” (The Dark Seal) for the Special International Honorable Mention in the “Poetry, Memory and Resistance” category.




The award committee informed Yıldız Çakar of its decision in a special letter. Highlighting the poet’s literary strength, the letter noted that she explores themes including violence against women, femicide, collective memory, land, loss and women’s resistance through a distinctive Kurdish perspective.




The letter also emphasized that Çakar’s poem expands the festival’s literary horizons beyond Latin America and the Caribbean, giving it a global dimension. It highlighted the work’s powerful connection to women’s struggles for freedom and dignity.

title: Koma Berxwedan: Release Nûdem Durak and ill prisoners
content:
Members of Koma Berxwedan and other artists issued a statement to draw attention to the situation of Kurdish artist Nûdem Durak, who has been in prison for 11.5 years and is reportedly battling serious illnesses.




Reacting to the 19-year-and-6-month prison sentence handed down to Nûdem Durak, the artists said that her health had deteriorated and that her life was in danger. They called for the release of all sick prisoners, particularly Nûdem Durak.




Criticising the continued imprisonment of sick prisoners at a time when the Peace and Democratic Society Process is being discussed, the artists called on human rights organisations, intellectuals, politicians and the public to intensify their efforts and raise their voices.







 







Freedom of ill prisoners must be our top priority




Speaking on behalf of Koma Berxwedan, Hekim Sefkan said that, at a time when hopes for peace were growing, decisions continued to be made that contradicted human rights and the spirit of the process. Reacting to the prison sentence imposed on Nûdem Durak, Sefkan said it was unacceptable that the artist was being kept behind bars despite her serious health problems.




Sefkan said: “At a time when hopes for peace are growing, decisions and actions that contradict human rights and the spirit of the process are also continuing. One such decision is the 19.5-year prison sentence imposed on

title: A border built with water: Six dams in succession
content:
There are six dams along a stretch of just 45–50 kilometers on the Ortasu (Rubozik) Stream, located on the border between Northern Kurdistan (Bakur) and Southern Kurdistan (Başur). Under normal circumstances, dams should either not be built because of the damage they cause to the ecological balance, or should only be constructed following an Environmental Impact Assessment for irrigation, flood prevention and electricity generation. However, these six dams serve a somewhat different purpose. The 2007 activity report of the State Hydraulic Works (DSI) states that their function is entirely security-related. This represents an unprecedented category worldwide, a new type of dam.




A look at the map reveals that all six dams have been built along a single stream. Each has its own tender, dam structure and reservoir. Yet for those living in the valley, they are all part of the same story: villages whose roads have been cut off, whose pastures and farmland have been lost, and whose residents face the winter fearing landslides and floods.




The fundamental question that needs to be asked is: Why does the Turkish state use dams so extensively as a security instrument in Kurdistan?




'Security dams': A new category

title: Akın: Policies destroying nature and society must end for ecological peace
content:
The Conference of the Parties (COP), held annually under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) to combat climate change, brings together countries from around the world. The 31st conference (COP31), which will address critical issues such as climate finance, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and the energy transition, will take place in Antalya from 9 to 20 November 2026.




However, the deepening ecological crisis despite nearly 30 years of conferences has reignited debate over the role of these summits in combating climate change. Ecologists are questioning whether these meetings offer genuine solutions for protecting nature and the climate.




Ibrahim Akın, Co-Deputy Chair of the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) responsible for Ecology and Agriculture, spoke about the importance of ecological peace in the context of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the background of the summit and the People's Climate Summit, which has emerged as an alternative gathering ahead of COP31.




'Ecological destruction impoverishes and displaces peoples'




Ibrahim Akın defined ecological peace as restoring balance in the relationship between humanity and nature and freeing nature and living environments from exploitation. He drew attention to the impact of ecological destruction on peoples and said: "Under capitalism, nature has been tran

title: DEM Party: Workplace deaths are consequence of a system of impunity that protects capital
content:
In a written statement, the Labour Commission recalled that on 8 November 2025, a fire broke out at a perfume-filling factory belonging to Ravive Kozmetik in the Dilovası district of Kocaeli. Seven workers, three of them children, lost their lives and six others were injured. “A year has passed. Yet, just as the pain of the families of the seven workers we lost has not subsided, their search for justice has still not yielded results,” the statement said.




The statement continued: “What happened in Dilovası was not a workplace accident, but the result of a model of production that disregards workers’ health and their right to life, of a lack of inspections, and of the capital’s insatiable pursuit of profit. This tragedy, which occurred at a workplace where children were allegedly employed under precarious conditions and where occupational safety measures were reportedly absent, has once again exposed the scale of exploitation in working life and the serious problems with regulatory and inspection mechanisms.”




The DEM Party underlined that “the demands of families who have lost their loved ones are clear, everyone bearing responsibility must be brought to trial, no defendant must receive preferential treatment, and justice must be delivered in every respect. This case is not only about employers. It must also establish how a workplace reportedly operating without a licence

title: Apoist prisoners: Fulfil the requirements of the process
content:
Apoist prisoners said in a statement: “Do not leave the Peace and Democratic Society Process at the level of rhetoric; fulfil its requirements! The physical freedom of our Leadership, along with the immediate release of all sick prisoners, is an issue on the agenda of this process that cannot be postponed.”




The statement added: “We, as political prisoners who have been held behind bars for years because of our ideas, our political identity and our commitment to our people's struggle for freedom, address our people and the public today.




The Peace and Democratic Society Process, initiated by our Leadership, represents a strategic shift and transformation aimed at rebuilding social life, political relations and approaches to struggle on democratic foundations. The transition from a strategy of armed struggle to one of democratic society and democratic politics places historical responsibilities on all social and political actors, above all the state and those in power. Concrete steps in keeping with the spirit of this process must be taken, the conflict-ridden conditions of the past must be overcome, and the way must be opened for a democratic solution.”

title: Whereabouts of KJAR members detained in Urmia unknown since June
content:
The Kurdistan Free Women’s Community (KJAR) announced that it has been unable to obtain any information about two of its members detained by Iranian security forces in Urmia.




In its statement on Sunday, KJAR reported that its member Zahra Pirdehghan (32) was detained by Iranian state forces on June 25, while another member, Parvin Rasegh Qizilbash (33), was detained on June 28. The organization described the detentions as a clear violation of human rights.




According to the statement, the families reported that despite the considerable time that had passed since the two women activists were detained, they had received no information about where they were being held, their health conditions, or their fate. Neither the security authorities nor judicial institutions provided any information regarding their situation.




KJAR warned that depriving its members of their rights to legal representation, regular communication, and contact with their families, as well as subjecting them to enforced disappearance, constituted violations of international law.




The organization demanded that the fate of its members be disclosed immediately and called for their fundamental rights, including access to medical examinations and communication, to be guaranteed.

title: ‘We cannot envision peace independently of any people or culture’
content:
As the Peace and Democratic Society Process continues, women came together to discuss the process and share their experiences of peacebuilding. Hundreds of women gathered at the “Women Side by Side, Discussing the Future” conference to address cultural, political, and social issues. Attended by women from various cities across Kurdistan and Turkey, the conference in Ankara explored women’s roles in peace processes and their ongoing efforts, as well as issues related to ecology and mother-tongue rights.




Painter Neşe Toprak, who attended the conference as a representative of the cultural sector, reflected on its atmosphere and outcomes. Emphasizing that efforts to embed peace in society must encompass all peoples and social groups, Toprak highlighted the importance of women, culture, ecology, and the struggle for mother-tongue rights in the process.




Toprak explained that the conference was organized to give concrete expression to women’s role as active participants in the process. Following nearly two months of preparation, it was held under the leadership of 82 organizing groups. The conference brought together participants from numerous cities across Turkey and from Europe, including women working to ensure that peoples can freely preserve and express their own languages, cultures, and civilizations.

title: Bayındır: The Turkish state must now take concrete steps
content:
The co-chair of the Democratic Regions Party (DBP), Keskin Bayındır, called on the Turkish government to finally take concrete legal and political measures in the ongoing peace process. “The end of the armed struggle does not mean that the Kurdish question has been resolved,” Bayındır said at an event in Götzis, Austria. Following the dissolution of the PKK and the decision to withdraw guerrilla forces, the Turkish state must now fulfill its responsibilities, he stated.




Murat Sarısaç, co-spokesperson of the DBP’s Diplomacy Commission, also attended the meeting at the Sara Cultural Association in the Austrian state of Vorarlberg. Discussions focused on the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey and political developments in South and West Kurdistan.

Democratic integration instead of assimilation

title: Culture and arts festival in Rome commemorates Nagihan Akarsel
content:
The 'Voce Arcaica' (Ancient Voice) Art and Culture Festival, organised annually in Italy by the Jineolojî Academy, was held in memory of Nagihan Akarsel, a member of the Jineolojî Research Centre, writer and journalist who was assassinated in an armed attack outside her home in Sulaymaniyah (Silêmanî) on 4 October 2022.




The festival took place on November 7 at the Teatro Biblioteca Quarticciolo in Rome. The morning program featured performances and sound and rhythm workshops focusing on the ancient voices of women. The activities, attended by Italian, Kurdish, and migrant women, explored women’s experiences of transforming sorrow, grief, and emotions into artistic expression.

Women’s voices and solidarity brought to the stage




The evening arts program featured music, dance, film, and theater performances. Inspired by the mulberry tree that Nagihan Akarsel loved, the stage was designed around a forest theme, conveying the message: “When one tree is cut down, we become a forest of ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’.”

title: Karacabey: Kurdish theatre is banned based on political risks
content:
Art in Turkey has faced censorship and repressive policies since the early years of the Republic. Theatre has also been subjected to the repression and censorship seen across many fields of artistic expression.




The struggle to produce political theatre continues in Turkey despite numerous obstacles, with political plays being banned and Kurdish-language productions unable to find stages. Meanwhile, Kurds and other communities living in Turkey who are regarded as the "other" are often represented on stage through negative characters.




ANF spoke to Associate Professor Süreyya Karacabey, an academic known for her work on theatre theory, playwriting and art criticism in Turkey, who was dismissed from her position by a statutory decree (KHK) in 2017. We discussed the state of theatre in Turkey, her assessments of the latest peace process and the role of art in the struggle for peace.




‘The desire to connect with society has a political dimension’




Süreyya Karacabey stated that theatre has a political dimension in a broader sense and pointed out that the struggle to establish a connection with society continues. She emphasised that political, social and economic conditions play a decisive role in shaping the theatrical environment.

title: Constitutional Court orders retrial of Mazlum İçli after ten years in prison
content:
Mazlum İçli has already spent more than ten years of his life in prison. He was accused of involvement, at the age of 14, in the killing of four people during the Kobanê protests in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) in October 2014. He was sentenced to a total of 124 years and eight months in prison. However, evidence that could exonerate him was not adequately considered during the trial. Turkey’s Constitutional Court has now confirmed serious deficiencies in the reasoning behind the verdict and ordered a retrial. İçli’s defense team intends to seek his immediate release.




The ruling, issued on September 16, 2026, could mark a decisive turning point in a case that has been fraught with contradictions for years. At the heart of the case is the question of why İçli was convicted despite several witnesses confirming that he was attending a wedding in the district of Kulp, approximately 140 kilometers away, at the time of the alleged crime. Video footage and an expert report also support his alibi.




The Constitutional Court particularly criticized the criminal court’s failure to provide a reasoned assessment of conflicting expert reports. While one examination suggested that İçli might be identifiable in footage from the crime scene, another report by the same expert confirmed with a high degree of probability that he was present at the wedding. title: Women organize symposium on social memory and trauma in Amed
content:
A symposium titled “Speaking Out: Social Memory, Testimony and Trauma” began at the Ali Emiri Conference Hall in cooperation with Amed Metropolitan Municipality, the Trauma Studies Association, and the Forum for Social Peace and Freedom.




Speaking during a session titled “Waiting at Ground Zero: Trauma, Unresolved Grief and the Power of Testimony in Enforced Disappearances,” moderated by social worker İrfan Ekinci, Sebla Arcan, a member of the Human Rights Association’s (İHD) Commission on Disappearances in Custody, said, “A person experiencing trauma due to the disappearance of a loved one can neither move forward nor go back. They remain trapped in that moment.”




Highlighting the trauma caused by enforced disappearances, Arcan said, “The effects continue for two or three generations after an enforced disappearance. But other things are also passed down through generations in connection with enforced disappearances. A sense of justice, the determination to struggle, and the spirit of resistance are also transmitted. What is passed down from generation to generation is not only trauma and grief but also political consciousness.”




Emphasizing the importance of testimony, Sebla Arcan said, “Your account of what happened is denied. Some people come and take your child into custody, but when you go to inquire about their detention, the authorities deny it ever happened. De

title: Seriously ill prisoner Tuncer Sağlam dies in Ankara
content:
Seriously ill political prisoner Tuncer Sağlam died in Ankara on Saturday morning. Sağlam was arrested and imprisoned in 2024 in the province of Van on charges of “propaganda for a terrorist organization.” Due to his critical health condition, he had most recently been receiving treatment at Etlik Hospital in Ankara, where he died after 25 days of treatment.




Sağlam was initially held at Van High-Security Prison. After his health deteriorated significantly, he was transferred to Sincan Prison No. 2 in the Turkish capital, Ankara, on October 9. His condition continued to worsen during his subsequent hospitalization, and he eventually had to be intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation.




Following the completion of the autopsy, Tuncer Sağlam’s body is expected to be transferred to his hometown of Van, where he will be laid to rest.

title: Mihemed: Women’s participation in decision making is a fundamental guarantee for future Syria
content:
Ruksen Mihemed, spokesperson for the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ), emphasized that guaranteeing the rights of Syrian women and enhancing their presence in decision-making positions constitute a fundamental pillar of any political process aimed at building a democratic, pluralistic Syria. She stressed the necessity of recognizing women’s roles and sacrifices, as well as ensuring their meaningful inclusion in shaping the country’s future.




​Ruksen Mihemed stated that over fifteen years of struggle and endeavor, the YPJ has played a historic role in transforming the reality of women and elevating their status in society. She noted that the units’ journey was not limited to military action and societal defense, but extended to empowering women in political, social, educational, and military fields, establishing their role as key partners in decision-making.
















​

Women’s Protection Units: Fifteen years of struggle and empowerment




​ Ruksen Mihemed explained that the establishment of the Women’s Protection Units marked a pivotal turning point in women’s resistance, proving that women possess the ability to protect themselves, organize their ranks, and assume responsibilities across various walks of life.

title: Final declaration of the Conference on the Social Institutionalization of Women’s Policies
content:
Women’s policies in Kurdish municipalities are no longer to be limited to individual institutions or social services but are intended to shape every aspect of municipal self-governance. This was one of the key outcomes of the Conference on the Social Institutionalization of Women’s Policies, held on November 2 and 3 in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır). In a final declaration published following the event, participants outlined a comprehensive program to rebuild municipal women’s structures, promote women’s economic self-determination, and ensure their organized participation in political decision-making.




Organized by the Women’s Council of Democratic Local Administrations and hosted by Amed Metropolitan Municipality, the conference was held under the slogan “Through Production and Organizing, We Embed Our Women’s Struggle in Society.” Through a total of 21 resolutions, the participating women’s organizations aim to establish a new organizational, financial, and social foundation for municipal women’s policies.




This approach is also shaped by years of state intervention in Kurdish municipal politics. The appointment of government trustees led to the closure of numerous women’s institutions, the abolition of independent municipal programs for women, and the dismantling of structures built up over many years. author: Unknown
title: Martyrs of Kurdistan’s Freedom Struggle commemorated in Sine
content:
Following the HPG’s announcement of the identities of nine guerrillas from Rojhilatê Kurdistan who fell as martyrs in the freedom struggle in previous years, a memorial event was held in the city of Sanandaj (Sine).







During the commemoration, the Martyrs’ Families Committee and Peace Mothers carried photographs of the fallen guerrillas and repeatedly chanted the slogan “Şehîd namirin” (Martyrs never die).







 







At the event, organised by the Martyrs’ Families Committee and the Peace Mothers, it was stated that the martyrs had become symbols of unity among all parts of Kurdistan.







It was also emphasised that the martyrs of the freedom struggle, from Kobanê, Shengal, Amed, Qamishlo and Hewraman to Sine, had set an example of defending humanity against ISIS.




At the end of the ceremony, the Martyrs’ Families Committee of Rojhilatê Kurdistan extended its condolences to the people of Sine and the patriotic people of Kurdistan. The committee also reiterated that the martyrs of Rojhilatê Kurdistan are martyrs of the entire Kurdish people.

author: Unknown
title: Laura Quagliuolo: Öcalan's freedom is key to lasting peace
content:
The Call for Peace and a Democratic Society issued by Abdullah Öcalan on 27 February 2025 brought discussions on a democratic solution to the Kurdish question into a new phase. International calls for Öcalan's freedom and the implementation of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) ruling on the "right to hope" also continue. Demands for Turkey to fulfill its obligations under the supervision of the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers are increasingly coming to the fore.




Italian feminist activist, writer and member of the Rete Jin women's solidarity network Laura Quagliuolo spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the importance of Öcalan's freedom for a democratic solution, the failure to implement ECtHR rulings and the role of women in building peace.




Efforts to find a democratic solution to the Kurdish question have continued since the call issued by Abdullah Öcalan on 27 February 2025. How do you assess the process at its current stage? What do you think are the fundamental conditions that must be met to achieve lasting peace?




I think the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey has not yet been realized. We have not reached that point yet, primarily because Abdullah Öcalan is not free. I believe Öcalan's freedom is a very important condition for the Kurdish people to achieve freedom and for their existence to be recognized.

title: KJK: The time for self-defence is now!
content:

Emphasising the importance of strengthening women's organisation and unity against male-dominated violence, the KJK stated that the Peace and Democratic Society Process would create new opportunities for women's free participation and their struggle for freedom.




The statement said: "Violence against women has never before been carried out with such depth and systematic intensity. Male-dominated violence, which has reached horrific levels and permeates every month, every day and every moment of the year, has made it imperative to say ‘enough is enough’. In this regard, effective results can only be achieved if we, as women, unite in organised struggle against femicide, the destruction of life, society and nature perpetrated by capitalist modernity — the representative of our era's murderous system of domination — and its derivatives, which inject these forms of destruction into every cell of life.




Against a culture of violence embedded in every aspect of social life, we, as women, need plans and projects that establish a multidimensional perspective of struggle, ranging from transforming the organisation of everyday life and relationships to building alternative structures for a free life. title: KNK warns of division in South Kurdistan and calls on KDP and PUK to engage in dialogue
content:
The Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) has warned of further divisions among Kurdish institutions amid the escalating government crisis in South Kurdistan. Following the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan’s (PUK) announcement that it would withdraw from the regional government and its threat to establish parallel administrative structures in Sulaymaniyah, the KNK called on the two dominant parties in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI), the KDP and PUK, to resume negotiations without delay. It stressed that political power struggles must no longer be conducted at the expense of the population and the region’s constitutionally guaranteed autonomy.




The latest escalation was triggered by Wednesday’s election of a new parliamentary leadership in Hewlêr (Erbil). After nearly two years of political deadlock, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), together with smaller parties and minority representatives, pushed ahead with the parliamentary session. The PUK and several opposition parties boycotted the vote because no agreement had been reached on the future distribution of power. With 52 of the 100 members of parliament participating, the session barely secured the required majority. KDP politician Vala Fareed was elected speaker of parliament.

title: Dismissed by decree and imprisoned, Engin Cengiz returns to music at MKM
content:
More than 125,000 public employees were dismissed from their positions through emergency decrees issued under the state of emergency declared after the attempted coup on 15 July 2016. While the government defended these measures as actions targeting those involved in the coup attempt, the process also paved the way for the dismissal of public employees opposed to the government.




Ten years have passed since the emergency decrees were issued. Many of those dismissed were imprisoned, some were forced into exile, while others remained unemployed for long periods. Some were forced to work in construction to make a living, and some lost their lives in workplace accidents.




Engin Cengiz, who now works as a music teacher at the Mesopotamia Cultural Center (MKM), was among those affected during this period, when 125,678 public employees were dismissed according to official figures.




Cengiz was dismissed from his position as a music teacher by an emergency decree in 2016 and was subsequently imprisoned for a period. He spoke to ANF about his experiences during the emergency decree period, the difficulties he faced after his dismissal and how he became involved with the Mesopotamia Cultural Center.







 







‘The turning point came after a two-day strike during the Kobane protests’

content:
Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Women's Council Spokesperson Halide Türkoğlu held a press conference at the party's headquarters ahead of the Women's Council meeting.




Türkoğlu began her speech by commemorating former Women's Council member Nesrin Aslan with respect and longing. She said that the women's conference would produce a powerful document for the success of the process. Women have demonstrated with strong determination that they are present in resistance, in struggle and at the negotiating table, and that no process can be shaped without women."




Türkoğlu once again welcomed the "Women Stand Together, Discussing the Future" conference, held in Ankara on 31 October and 1 November, saying that it had been organized "in this spirit." She added: "We wholeheartedly believe that the outcomes of this conference will constitute a powerful document for the success of the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Women already have their roadmap for peace and are ready to build their present and future."




Support for the Peace Mothers' demands

author: Unknown
title: KCDP: 20 women murdered in October
content:
The We Will Stop Femicide Platform (KCDP) has published its October 2026 report on femicides, stating that at least 20 women were murdered, and 39 others lost their lives under suspicious circumstances.




Of the 20 women murdered, five were killed by their husbands, four by their current partners, one by someone they knew, one by their father, four by their former husbands and two by their former partners. The relationship between the perpetrators and the remaining three women could not be established. The report noted that 25 percent of the women were murdered by their husbands.




Nine women were murdered in their homes, three in the street, two in cars, two at their workplaces and one in a recreational area. The location of the murders of three women could not be determined. According to the report, 45 percent of the women murdered in October were killed in their homes.

title: Tuğba Hezer: Women must have a direct say in negotiations
content:
Kurdish politician Tuğba Hezer spoke about the social dimension of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the role of women in the process and the struggle for women's rights. Hezer drew attention to the exclusion of women from decision-making mechanisms in previous peace processes and Kurdish women's struggle for their identity and language. She said that women must have a direct say and decision-making power in negotiations.




Hezer highlighted the devastation caused by war and social inequalities in women's lives, the denial of women's identity and their exclusion from peace processes.




Hezer said: "Women bear the heaviest consequences of war, conflict and social inequalities. Yet throughout history, decisions in peace processes have largely been made without women. The denial of women's identity in Turkey, particularly Kurdish women's struggle to exist with their own mother tongue, identity and as women, cannot be separated from the devastation caused by war. Women experience the destruction of war while also facing patriarchal state violence. We struggle against these inequalities in every sphere, from politics and education to public and social life.




A different approach is needed in this process. We cannot accept women being treated merely as people whose demands are heard and on whose behalf decisions are made. If we are going to call it a negotiating table,

author: Unknown
title: Lawyer Newroz Uysal Aslan: Real change will come when Mr. Öcalan can engage with the outside world
content:
The relocation of Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan within Imrali F-Type High Security Prison has brought discussions about his status back into focus. Presidential adviser Mehmet Uçum's tendency to reduce the status of Abdullah Öcalan, the chief negotiator in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, solely to "disarmament" has drawn widespread criticism. The disagreement over Öcalan's status, one of the most important aspects of the process, came to the fore once again after Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP Ömer Öcalan, who recently visited his uncle on Imrali, reported that Öcalan opposed this restrictive approach and criticized attempts to address the process solely in terms of disarmament. DEM Party MP Newroz Uysal Aslan spoke to ANF and recalled that Abdullah Öcalan's status was that of chief negotiator. Uysal said: "The change in Mr. Öcalan's conditions must go beyond discussions about relocation and place him in a position where he can genuinely engage with society and guide the process."




'Relocation does not mean Mr. Öcalan's conditions are adequate'




Newroz Uysal Aslan said that Abdullah Öcalan's relocation within Imrali Prison was significant but insufficient to meet the needs of the process. Uysal stressed that the relocation should have taken place at the beginning of the process and had therefore been delayed. Uysal said: "We canno

title: Bafel Talabani: We are withdrawing from this government
content:
The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) Executive Council convened with the participation of its President, Bafel Talabani. Following the meeting, Talabani released a video statement in which he commented on political developments in the Kurdistan Region and the process of forming a government.




Talabani stated that they had held several meetings with officials in Erbil (Hewlêr), but despite progress in the discussions, no agreement had been reached and parliament had been unable to convene. “On every occasion, progress was made in the discussions, but no results were achieved, and parliament could not convene. It has been demonstrated that the KDP does not know how to govern. We had previously warned that such a situation would arise. We do not recognise this session,” Talabani said.




‘We are withdrawing from this government’

content:

title: Osman: Over 238 children killed or injured in military attacks in Bashur over the past 30 years
content:
Kameran Osman, a member of the Community Peacemaker Teams (CPT), spoke at a panel titled “Being a Victim of War, Crisis and Displacement During Childhood”, held as part of the International Scientific Conference on Children and Youth at the University of Sulaymaniyah (Silêmani).




Speaking about the impact of war on children, Osman shared new data. He said that more than 238 children have been killed or injured in military attacks by the Turkish and Iranian armies in the Kurdistan Region over the past 30 years. He emphasised that the effects of war on children are not limited to physical casualties.




He noted that children displaced by war often lose or see their ties weakened with the countries, communities and lands where they live. Osman also highlighted how war deeply affects children's mental health, identity, education, language and dignity.




People in border villages still wake up to the sound of bombs




Osman recalled that schools and educational institutions in villages have also been targeted in military attacks by the Turkish army and Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), stating that children's safety has been disregarded.

author: Unknown
title: Gülten Kaya: Art requires the courage to engage with life
content:
Gülten Kaya has always been at the heart of music, poetry and stories of her homeland, both through her own personal journey and as Ahmet Kaya's life partner and Yusuf Hayaloğlu's sister.




Gülten Kaya, with whom we discussed the transformation of the music world, said that digital platforms also generated ethical and moral problems of their own. She identified creating works in one's mother tongue as one of the most important pillars of collective memory.




Gülten Kaya said of Ahmet Kaya's music: "It is socially conscious, it bears witness, it is authentic, literary, recent history, poetry, emotion and sacrifice. His music reflects both recent history and all the suffering experienced by society." She also criticized the reduction of art to an apolitical industry: "All creative fields, from painting to literature, cinema to music, require the courage to engage with life. Art is one of the fields in which the greatest courage is needed to bear witness to life, particularly in countries like ours."




ANF spoke to lyricist and music producer Gülten Kaya about the transformation of the music world and the impact of digitalization on music production and consumption habits.




The music industry has evolved toward a digitalized, algorithm-driven market model in recent years. How is this transforming music's role in creating collective memory and fostering social empathy?

title: Nurcan Değirmenci: As women, we must stand together
content:
Musician and activist Nurcan Değirmenci, who performed at the "Women Stand Together, Discussing the Future" conference held in Ankara on 31 October and 1 November, spoke about women's role in art and social peace and called on women to stand together in public squares on 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.




Nurcan Değirmenci said that she began her artistic career at the Mesopotamia Cultural Center in 1995 and had struggled shoulder to shoulder with women for many years, both as a musician and as a Kurdish woman. She recalled that they established the Art for Peace Initiative (BIS) in 2009, bringing artistic production together with the struggle for peace.




Değirmenci said, "Art is an indispensable element in the existence of culture," and emphasizing that the search and struggle for identity also involved artistic resistance.




'Women will shape the language of peace'




Nurcan Değirmenci said that the central message of the conference, for her, was the importance of women standing together without denying their own stories. She expressed her belief that women would build the language of peace in this period. title: DEM Party: Abolish the Council of Higher Education, a vestige of the 1980 military coup
content:

The statement said: “Established on 6 November 1981, in the aftermath of the 12 September military coup, the Council of Higher Education (YÖK) has continued for 45 years to be one of the principal institutions through which a centralised and tutelary system of governance is imposed on universities.”




The statement noted that, particularly under AKP rule, this structure had become one of the instruments through which the political authorities intervened in university affairs, and added: “It is unacceptable that young people are pushed out of politics, that their freedoms of association and expression are restricted, and that universities are transformed into institutions that produce obedient individuals. Young people are not merely the social and political actors of the future; they are actors in society and politics today.”




The DEM Commission outlined the kind of university it envisions as follows:

title: Nilüfer Koç: Council of Europe must consider the new process
content:
A total of 845 signatures from 50 countries have been collected as part of the "Freedom for Abdullah Öcalan, a Political Solution to the Kurdish Question" campaign. International support, including that of 109 Nobel Prize laureates, has been brought to the Council of Europe. Most recently, 620 signatories from 29 countries sent a letter to the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers.




ANF spoke to Nilüfer Koç, Co-Spokesperson for Foreign Relations of the Kurdistan National Congress (KNK), about the results of the international campaign, diplomatic initiatives to be pursued at the Council of Europe, steps toward implementing the right to hope, and upcoming efforts aimed at securing Abdullah Öcalan's physical freedom.

title: Executions and prison sentences continue in Iran
content:
The Kurdistan Human Rights Organisation has published a report on Iran’s repression of Rojhilatê Kurdistan (Eastern Kurdistan) and Iranian citizens.




The report states that courts in Tehran and Mashhad have sentenced five protesters, Alireza Rezai, Vahid Kehermani, Mehdi Jalali, Metin Şebani and Emir Dilşad, to death. All five were arrested during the January 2026 protests.




According to the report, all five were convicted of “collaborating with enemy states”. Two female prisoners tried in the same case, whose identities have yet to be established, were each sentenced to 30 years in prison.




Mehdi Jalali, who previously served as an imam, was reportedly sentenced to death by the Special Court for Clerics on charges of apostasy.




Meanwhile, 19 religious scholars held in Urmia Central Prison (Yakup Muradi, Ibrahim Jiyani, Areş Agahi, Esed Muhammediyan, Awine Kaytarani, Çiya Nasrullahi, Resul Yusuf, Siyamend Alipur, Hemin Ahmedi, Emin Dilnişin, Şehriyar Hızır, Cafer, Vezir Zersaw, Rahim Asare, Afşin, Areş Kulizade, Mihran Nirumendi, Kamyar Şeyhi and Mevlud Ateşbar, as well as Saadet Taşke) have reportedly been sentenced to prison terms ranging from six to ten months.




The report also states that the prisoners have been denied leave, limited freedoms and the right to receive medical treatment outside the prison.

title: MKG: Repression against women journalists continued in October
content:
According to the October 2026 report on rights violations published by the Mesopotamia Women Journalists Association (MKG), one woman journalist was arrested and imprisoned, two women journalists were detained, and another journalist’s home was raided in Turkey last month. In addition, one woman journalist was subjected to ill-treatment, and one incident of obstruction of news coverage was documented.




The report stated that an investigation was launched against one woman journalist, another was sentenced to 18 months in prison, and nine women journalists continued to face trial in nine separate cases. It emphasized that prosecuting journalists for reporting on violence and rights violations against women constituted an infringement of the public’s right to information.




Digital censorship and dismissals




Highlighting the continued digital censorship targeting the free press, the report documented the blocking of two websites and restrictions on access to 20 news articles. It stated that these measures made it more difficult for information about rights violations against women to reach the public.




The report noted that 162 journalists lost their jobs. However, it was not possible to determine how many of them were women. MKG drew attention to the precarious working conditions and discrimination faced by women journalists.

title: Ciwan İbrahim is Rojava
content:
“I am a child of Serêkaniyê. My mother’s name is Enisa, and my father’s name is Abdurrahim. Who are you? Where do you come from?” These were the words Ciwan İbrahim addressed to the militants of Jabhat al-Nusra. It was 2012, and the battle for Serêkaniyê was underway. Despite being wounded in the hand, Ciwan refused even to have his injury bandaged and would not abandon his fighters. “If I withdraw, my comrades will be affected. I am putting all my strength into this battle,” he said, as he considered how to continue directing the fighting with his other hand.




Ciwan İbrahim’s 18-year journey, stretching from Serêkaniyê to Lebanon, from Garê to the resistance tunnels of Zap and the Rojava Revolution, was marked by this determination. Throughout this journey, he distinguished himself at different times as an accomplished journalist, a commander, and one of the leading figures among the people.




Some of us came to know him when he announced the establishment of the People’s Defense Units (YPG), others as a commander of the Asayish (Internal Security Forces), and still others as he rode his motorcycle through the streets of Qamişlo.




Today, Rojava mourns the loss of this legendary commander.




From Lebanon to the mountains of Kurdistan

title: Veysi Aktaş: A struggle disconnected from society cannot succeed
content:
What role can literature, language, and intellectuals play in shaping a democratic peace? This question is at the heart of an international conference that began on Friday in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır). Under the title “The Role of Literature, Language and intelligentsia in Processes of Dialogue, Reconciliation, Peace and Equality,” writers, academics, and representatives of civil society organizations and political parties have come together. Discussions focus on the social responsibility of cultural figures, the freedom of the Kurdish language, and the prospects of the Peace and Democratic Society Process.




The event, held at the Ali Emiri Conference Hall, is organized by the international writers’ association PEN, the Kurdish PEN Center (PENa Kurd), Amed Metropolitan Municipality, and the district municipalities of Sur, Yenişehir, Bağlar, and Kayapınar. It began with a moment of silence.







Peace requires linguistic and cultural freedom




At the opening, Ömer Fidan, a writer and chair of PENa Kurd, stated that literary figures must take responsibility for building a dignified peace. He said the conference aimed to strengthen the social and cultural dimensions of the peace process.

title: IHD documents hundreds of human rights violations in Turkish prisons
content:
The Human Rights Association (IHD) documented a total of 899 human rights violations in Turkish prisons between July and September 2026. The most frequently reported violations concerned access to food and drinking water, protection against ill-treatment, and the right to communication. The organization warned of a further deterioration in prison conditions and accused the Turkish government of allowing problems to persist even when they could be easily resolved.




The report on the human rights situation in prisons across the Marmara region was presented at a press conference held at the IHD branch office in Istanbul’s Beyoğlu district. Gülseren Yoleri, a member of the IHD Central Executive Board, Meral Nergis Şahin, co-spokesperson for the Prison Commission, and commission member Sevilay Yılmaz Birgin took part in the presentation.




The investigation was based on complaints and submissions from prisoners and their relatives, as well as publicly available information. The report noted that prisons were operating beyond their designated capacities.




Ill-treatment and inadequate living conditions




Most of the documented rights violations concerned prisoners’ basic living conditions. In 293 cases, the IHD recorded inadequate access to food and clean drinking water, as well as deficiencies in hygiene and personal care. Another 258 violations involved physical assaults,

title: Court overturns fine imposed on Syriac Orthodox church in İdil
content:
The Syriac Orthodox Church of the Virgin Mary in İdil district of Şırnak province has secured a preliminary legal victory against the AKP-run municipality. The Şırnak Administrative Court has suspended the enforcement of a fine of approximately 1.17 million Turkish lira (around 20,800 euros), which had been imposed on the church foundation over a guesthouse allegedly built without a permit. The main proceedings are still ongoing.




In June, the municipality imposed an administrative fine of 1,170,743.24 lira on the foundation of the historic Syriac Orthodox Church of the Virgin Mary and sealed the guesthouse in October. The foundation subsequently challenged the measure in court.




In its ruling, the Administrative Court found that the municipality had failed to adequately investigate who had actually constructed the building in question. According to the court, the mere fact that the building lacked a construction permit was not sufficient to hold the church foundation responsible.




The court criticized the incomplete examination of the facts and ordered the suspension of the fine without requiring a security deposit. As a result, it concluded, the penalty cannot be enforced until further notice. A final decision on its legality has yet to be made.

title: Journalist Haşim Abak detained in Mardin
content:
Kurdish journalist Haşim Abak, a reporter for the Mezopotamya News Agency (MA), was detained on Tuesday night in the district of Nusaybin in Mardin province. Abak was traveling in a vehicle when he was stopped by police.




Necla Özgezer and a 16-year-old identified by the initials H. T. were also taken into custody alongside him. On Wednesday morning, the three were transferred to the Mardin Police Headquarters and handed over to the Counterterrorism Department (TEM).




They are expected to be questioned later in the day. No information has yet been provided regarding the reasons for their detention.

An expert report published by Mediendienst Integration on 15 October 2026, titled Kurds in Germany: Between Asylum, Social Participation and Anti-Kurdish Racism, examines the demographic situation of Kurds in the country, asylum procedures, social participation and experiences of discrimination.




The expert study underpinning the report was prepared by Professor Çinur Ghaderi of the Protestant University of Applied Sciences Bochum (EvH Bochum). The study was supported by the Robert Bosch Foundation.




The Munich component of the research examined the living conditions of Kurds and their experiences of racism in detail. The study, prepared by Professor Çinur Ghaderi, Monique Kaulertz and Mary Lam, was conducted at the request of the Democracy Unit (Fachstelle für Demokratie) of the City of Munich.




183 out of 210 respondents reported experiencing discrimination




The Munich study, conducted in 2025 and published in January 2026, revealed the extent of discrimination faced by Kurds in the city. The research included a quantitative survey involving 210 participants, alongside 23 individual expert interviews and nine focus group discussions. Approximately 65 people participated in the focus group discussions.

title: Özdal: Ruling elites openly robbed large sections of society
content:
The economic and political repercussions of the financial developments that erupted in Turkey in September and became known publicly as the "fund crisis" continue to be debated. Allegations have emerged that numerous individuals, including figures affiliated with the Justice and Development Party (AKP), obtained illicit profits through investment funds.




Some figures released in connection with the crisis suggest that losses may have reached as much as 2.7 trillion Turkish liras. Investigations involving the names of AKP figures and state officials have intensified public debate, while criticism of the government's handling of the crisis has also grown. President Tayyip Erdoğan's latest remarks on the fund crisis have been interpreted as an indication of growing discontent over the developments even among AKP supporters.




Journalist Hakkı Özdal spoke to ANF about the causes of the fund crisis, the relationship between political authorities and financial circles, the role of international capital and the crisis's potential impact on society.




'The bubble economists and journalists had warned about has burst'

content:
Lawyer Mehtap Sakinci, one of the founders of the 10 October Peace Association, spoke to ANF about peace, justice and the women's struggle on the 11th anniversary of the 10 October Ankara Train Station Massacre.




Sakinci said that femicide was political and criticized Turkey's withdrawal from the Istanbul Convention and the shortcomings in the implementation of Law No. 6284. She stressed that women played an important role in building peace and called on women to stand together and strengthen their struggle ahead of 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

title: 12th edition of Serçavan Kurdish Film Days opens in Vienna
content:
The Serçavan Kurdish Film Days, which have been held at different intervals in Vienna since 1999, opened for the 12th time this year.




The festival, taking place at Votivkino, is organised in cooperation with the Assembly of the Kurdish Community in Austria (FEYKOM), the Union of Kurdish Students (YXK), and partner organisations.




The five-day festival, running from 4 to 8 November, features a programme of feature films, documentaries and short films. Addressing Kurdish history, culture, identity, experiences of migration and contemporary social realities, the films present audiences with a variety of perspectives and narratives.







 







The festival opened with the documentary 

To My Sisters

, which tells the stories of Kurdish women fighters and their struggle for freedom. Following the screening, the director took part in an online question-and-answer session and responded to questions from the audience.




Kurds must tell their own stories

title: 'Voce Arcaica' Festival in memory of Nagihan Akarsel to take place in Rome on 7 November
content:
The 'Voce Arcaica' (Ancient Voice) Art and Culture Festival, organised annually in Italy by the Jineolojî Academy, is held in memory of Nagihan Akarsel, a member of the Jineolojî Research Centre, writer and journalist who was assassinated in an armed attack outside her home in Sulaymaniyah (Silêmanî) on 4 October 2022.




The festival will take place on 7 November at the Teatro Biblioteca Quarticciolo in Rome, and aims to bring women together through art, culture and collective creation.




In an 

article

, the Jineolojî Academy wrote that the festival was organised to continue the work of Nagihan Akarsel, who made significant contributions to Jineolojî, women's journalism and research on women, and to keep her ideas alive through art.




The article emphasised that art is not merely a form of expression, but also a means of passing on women's collective memory, resistance and experiences of struggle.




Four stops on the festival's journey




As part of this year's third edition, events have been held throughout the year in Rome, Reggio Calabria, Turin, Bologna and the Dutch town of Haelen. At these gatherings, the book 

Voce Arcaica

 (Ancient Voice), a collection of 16 articles by Nagihan Akarsel, was introduced. Participants also took part in a collective embroidery project featuring a portrait of Nagihan Akarsel.

title: Hope lies with young people
content:
Our generation grew up under the influence of the 1968 Youth Revolution. More precisely, we were forged in the fire of that historic revolution. The Revolutionary Youth Movement of 1968 was based primarily on university students. It was the most striking example of conscious, organised youth taking the lead in society as a whole. Through this revolutionary movement, university students proved themselves and passed the test of history.




The 1968 Youth Revolution was the most influential revolutionary wave since the 1917 Soviet Revolution, which emerged during the First World War. It aimed not only to overthrow the system of capitalist modernity, whose crisis was deepening, but also to transcend actually existing socialism, which had moved away from the principles of equality based on freedom and diversity. For various reasons, it undoubtedly failed to overthrow the system of capitalist modernity. However, it played a significant role in the collapse of actually existing socialism, which had proved incapable of correcting or renewing itself. Had actually existing socialism understood the revolution developed by intellectual university youth, and demonstrated the capacity to transform and renew itself on the basis of that revolution's characteristics, perhaps it would not have met the tragic end it did, nor disintegrated in that way.

title: The anatomy of special warfare and paths to youth liberation in the Middle East
content:
Special warfare is not an overt military operation carried out with tanks and artillery. It is a system of psychological and social destruction that directly targets society's consciousness, culture and moral values. Within this system, the most strategic targets of dominant and colonial powers are young people and young women. This is because youth is the dynamic driving force of social transformation, while young women are the founding subjects of a free society. The state mentality and dominant powers seek first and foremost to paralyze this revolutionary and pioneering force in order to permanently establish their hegemony over the will of peoples.




As Abdullah Öcalan, whose ideas have become central to the political and philosophical discussions of the Kurdish people, the Middle East and peoples around the world, has strongly emphasized, unless a radical consciousness of "self-defense" is developed against this systematic process of social degradation, society will be completely severed from its historical and moral foundations.




The following sections examine, point by point, the reality into which young people have been pushed, the social destruction caused by the instruments of degradation described as the "three horsemen of the apocalypse," and the paths to liberation, with the aim of providing every young person with a guide to action.

title: Iran attacks Komala base in Balîsan
content:
Iran attacked a base belonging to the Komeleya Şoreşgerên Zehmetkêşên Kurdistanê (Association of Revolutionary Toilers of Kurdistan) in Balîsan, southern Kurdistan, this morning. According to the party, the attack took place at around 8:40 a.m. and involved two explosive-laden drones.




Komala stated that no one was injured or killed in the attack northeast of Hewlêr (Erbil). However, the organization reported that the attack caused significant damage to property at the base.




Since the outbreak of the war between Iran, the United States, and Israel, Tehran has repeatedly attacked targets in various parts of southern Kurdistan. More than 30 people have reportedly been killed in these attacks so far.

author: Unknown
title: Students demanding education in mother tongue attacked in Hesekê
content:
A demonstration demanding the right to education in the mother tongue was attacked in the northeastern Syrian city of Hesekê. Students had gathered outside the provincial administration building to demand education in their own language. Forces affiliated with the Syrian transitional government intervened against the gathering and fired shots into the air.




According to information obtained by the ANHA news agency, a group believed to be Arab residents from the Xiwêran neighborhood initially attacked the demonstrators with stones. Meanwhile, security forces of the transitional government attempted to disperse the protest and prevent it from continuing, using firearms.




The students condemned the intervention and emphasized the peaceful nature of their demonstration. “What have we done wrong to be prevented from doing this? We took to the streets peacefully and are demanding our right to our own language,” they told ANHA. The protesters also made it clear that the attacks would not deter them from demanding education in their mother tongue.




Since early September, students and their families in Rojava have been protesting against restrictions on Kurdish-language education. The protests were triggered by the Syrian transitional government’s decision to scale back Kurdish-language instruction and limit Kurdish classes to three hours per week. title: Hatimoğulları visits Demirtaş, calls for the release of political prisoners
content:
Ten years after the crackdown on the Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP), Tülay Hatimoğulları, Co-Chair of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), called for the release of all political prisoners in Turkey. Following a visit to former HDP Co-Chair Selahattin Demirtaş, who has been imprisoned since November 2016, at Edirne Prison, she declared that the struggle would continue until no one remained behind bars for political reasons.




The subsequent rally outside the prison was attended by numerous supporters and representatives of left-wing and socialist parties, including Seyit Aslan, Chair of the Labour Party (EMEP).




The gathering marked the tenth anniversary of November 4, 2016, when the Turkish government launched a sweeping crackdown on the parliamentary representation of the Kurdish population with the arrests of the HDP’s co-chairs and several other members of parliament.

Hatimoğulları called for the immediate release of Selahattin Demirtaş and Figen Yüksekdağ and all those imprisoned in connection with the Kobanê trial. She demanded the implementation of the rulings of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR).

title: Kurdistan Region Parliament elects presidency
content:
The first session of the Kurdistan Region Parliament’s sixth term began earlier today after the required quorum was reached with the participation of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and several other parliamentarians.




As Mihemed Silêman of the New Generation Movement and Azad Mihemedemîn of the PUK were absent, KDP member Semîra Hesen, the oldest parliamentarian present, presided over the session.




During the session, held without the participation of the PUK (Patriotic Union of Kurdistan), candidates were nominated for the positions of Speaker, Deputy Speaker, and Parliamentary Secretary.




In a joint statement issued yesterday, the KDP parliamentary group and the Turkmen Reform Party called on all parliamentarians to attend today’s parliamentary session. The Presidency of the Kurdistan Region Parliament announced that only 43 parliamentarians had signed the request for the session and that the meeting could not be held because the required quorum had not been reached.




Responding to the KDP’s call to convene parliament, the PUK stated: “In accordance with our deep commitment to the principles of the rule of law and national consensus, we believe that this meeting is illegal and constitutes an attempt by one side to impose its will.” The PUK also announced that it would not recognize any parliament or government formed following the session unless national con

title: Call for action on the anniversary of November 4 coup: Comply with ECtHR rulings, release prisoners!
content:
Civil society organizations, professional associations, and bar associations in the Kurdish region gathered outside the Diyarbakır Courthouse on the anniversary of the November 4, 2016 operations targeting the HDP.




During the gathering, participants unfurled a banner featuring photographs of politicians imprisoned in connection with the Kobanê trial. The banner read: “A requirement of the rule of law, a necessity for democracy: Freedom. Implement ECtHR rulings, pave the way for democratic politics.”




Diyarbakır Bar Association President Sertaç Buluttekin recalled that former HDP Co-Chairs Selahattin Demirtaş and Figen Yüksekdağ, along with HDP MPs, had been detained and unlawfully imprisoned in 2016.




Buluttekin said that Turkey had failed to implement the rulings of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) despite the Court’s findings of violations. He emphasized that the continued imprisonment of those imprisoned in connection with the Kobanê trial and the failure to enforce judicial decisions undermined public confidence in social peace.




In a joint statement read by Ercan Yılmaz, Co-Chair of the Diyarbakır branch of the Human Rights Association (İHD), the organizations stated that the Kobanê trial was part of broader efforts to undermine democratic politics through judicial means.

author: Unknown
title: Bakırhan visits Figen Yüksekdağ, calls for freedom for political prisoners
content:
Ten years after the wave of arrests targeting the Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP), representatives of several left-wing and democratic parties gathered outside Kandıra Women’s Prison in the western Turkish province of Kocaeli to demand the release of political prisoners. The gathering marked the anniversary of November 4, 2016, when the Turkish government launched a sweeping crackdown on the parliamentary representation of the Kurdish population with the arrests of then-HDP Co-Chairs Figen Yüksekdağ and Selahattin Demirtaş, along with several other members of parliament.




Tuncer Bakırhan, Co-Chair of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), had earlier visited Figen Yüksekdağ, who has been imprisoned for ten years, together with a delegation. Following the visit, party representatives and numerous supporters gathered outside the prison. Under the slogan “Freedom for political prisoners – for peace and democracy,” they demanded the release of those imprisoned.







Bakırhan: The political crackdown of 2016 continues to have repercussions today




Bakırhan described the arrests of November 4, 2016, as a “political coup” whose consequences have long since extended beyond the Kurdish opposition. He said the process had begun with the lifting of parliamentary immunity on May 20, 2016, a move that had also been supported by sections of the opposition at the time.

title: Peace Mothers: There can be no peace unless Abdullah Öcalan is free!
content:
The Peace Mothers, who traveled to Ankara from various cities across Kurdistan and Turkey, held meetings at the Turkish parliament on Tuesday. As part of their peace initiative, they met with representatives of several parliamentary groups, including the YENI Party, the Yeni Yol parliamentary group, the MHP, and the ruling AKP. The discussions focused on Abdullah Öcalan’s physical freedom, the release of political prisoners, and concrete measures to advance the Peace and Democratic Society Process.




The meetings followed the Peace Mothers’ gathering in the parliamentary park, where women from 24 cities held a peace vigil on Monday and called on political leaders to advance the Peace and Democratic Society Process through concrete measures.




After a press statement about their meetings, the mothers returned home yesterday, while a delegation representing them remained in Ankara for further talks.




As part of their meetings in parliament, the Peace Mothers met with Speaker of Parliament Numan Kurtulmuş on Wednesday. Peace Mothers Hanife Akpolat, Müzeyyen Bütün and Afife Kartal attended the meeting, which took place in the Speaker’s office. Following their meeting with Kurtulmuş, the mothers held a press statement outside parliament’s Dikmen Gate.




Speaking here, Peace Mother Müzeyyen Bütün said: “The meetings went well. We hope this process will reach a successful con

title: Kurdish writer Gülazer Akın released after 30 years in prison
content:
Kurdish political prisoner and writer Gülazer Akın has been released from Bünyan Women’s Prison in Turkey’s Kayseri province after 30 years of imprisonment. She was welcomed outside the prison by family members, representatives of the prisoners’ solidarity association TUHAYDER and numerous supporters. Akın, who had been imprisoned since November 1996, endured numerous health problems during her decades behind bars, completed a university degree and wrote several literary works.




Upon her release, Akın said she had not believed until the very end that she would actually be able to leave prison. The release of a fellow prisoner had previously been postponed by a decision of the Prison Administration and Observation Board. She therefore feared that her own release might also be blocked.




“As long as even one of our friends remains in prison, I will not feel that I have truly been released,” Akın said. She also welcomed the peace process that had begun: “We have matured and returned. A new process has begun. I said this before the board as well. A new process has begun, and I support it. There is probably nothing more beautiful than freedom.”




Following her remarks, Akın released a white dove as a symbol of peace.




TUHAY-DER calls for the release of political prisoners

title: Ecocide continues in Şırnak: Hundreds of oak trees cut down
content:
Environmental destruction continues in the Kurdish province of Şırnak. Footage recorded by local residents yesterday in the Besta region shows hundreds of oak trees cut down across a vast area, leaving large sections of the forest stripped of trees.




While activities carried out under the guise of mining exploration on Mount Cudi and oil exploration on Mount Gabar for nearly a decade have already caused significant environmental damage, tree felling continues in the Besta region under the pretext of commercial activity.




According to reports, oak trees, some of them up to a century old, have been cut down by village guards under military supervision. Footage recorded in the Kaniya Kolanan and Dergê Gêzna areas showed numerous trees being cut down at their bases with chainsaws. The logging site is reportedly accessible only through a military checkpoint, and around ten people were said to be operating in the area with vans and chainsaws.




DEM Party Şırnak MP Mehmet Zeki İrmez shared the footage on his social media account, condemning the tree felling and tagging the Şırnak Governor’s Office and the Provincial Directorate of Agriculture.

title: Vigil in Geneva enters its 69th month: ‘Öcalan’s status must be officially recognized’
content:
A vigil by the Democratic Kurdish Community in Switzerland has been taking place in front of the UN headquarters in Geneva since 25 January 2021. Every Wednesday, activists stage a protest in front of the United Nations building to demand the release of Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan. The action is carried out as part of the 'Dem dema azadiye' [Time for Freedom] campaign and is directed against the isolation of the Kurdish leader on the Turkish prison island of Imrali, the Turkish occupation attacks on Kurdistan, the massacres committed in Kurdish territories and the silence of the UN. Demonstratos call on international institutions to fulfill their responsibilities to secure Öcalan’s physical freedom.




This week's demonstration, which is held at a tent set up in Nations Square where the UN Office is located, began with a moment of silence in memory of those who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle.




During this week’s demonstration, participants from Kurdistan once again called on international institutions to fulfill their responsibilities in securing the physical freedom of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan, who has been held in Imralı Island Prison since 1999.

title: Rojhilat Alliance: Member parties in favor of continuing dialogue
content:
The Rojhilat Kurdistan Union Group issued a written statement regarding its meeting with representatives of four member parties of the Alliance of Political Forces of Eastern Kurdistan.




The statement said: “In order to activate the Alliance of Political Forces of Eastern Kurdistan, which was established more than eight months ago, and to identify the obstacles preventing it from functioning effectively, the Rojhilat Kurdistan Union Group invited the Alliance’s six parties to a consultative meeting.




The Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK), the Organization of Struggle of Iranian Kurdistan (Sazmana Xebat a Kurdistana Îranê), the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan (KDP-I), and the Association of Kurdistan Toilers attended the meeting.




Only the Komala Party stated that it was not prepared to attend the meeting. In addition, a few days before the meeting, the Democratic Party of Iranian Kurdistan (KDP-I) withdrew without providing any explanation.




On Sunday (1 November 2026), a three-hour meeting was held between the Rojhilat Kurdistan Union Group and representatives of four parties belonging to the Alliance of Political Forces of Eastern Kurdistan.”

title: German ambassador visits Amed Metropolitan Municipality
content:
The German Ambassador to Turkey, Sibylle Katharina Sorg, visited Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) Metropolitan Municipality. Accompanied by Embassy Secretary Nicole Gonsior, she was received by Serra Bucak and Emin Ay, the co-mayors of the DEM Party-run metropolitan municipality.

The discussions focused on the work of the local administration, ongoing projects in the city, and opportunities for mutual cooperation. No details were provided regarding specific initiatives or agreements.

The meeting was also attended by the municipality’s Secretary General, Serdar Bakıroğlu, and Deputy Secretary General, Muhabbet Erdoğmuş. The co-mayors thanked the ambassador for her visit.

title: Ağın: A united struggle is needed to democratise Turkey - Part One
content:
Writer and politician Ömer Ağın stated that the main obstacle to the Peace and Democratic Society Process was the state's failure to take concrete steps towards a democratic solution.




Ağın emphasised that democratic mass organisations, trade unions and professional associations must join the struggle for the process to advance, highlighting the importance of uniting around current democratic demands.




Ömer Ağın recalled the historical roots of the Kurdish question and the state's security-oriented approach, stating that a solution required time and mutual determination. Ağın said, "This process involves longstanding difficulties and deep-rooted problems. The Kurdish question is undoubtedly one of Turkey's most important and complex issues."




Ağın continued: "The issue has historical roots, and there are grievances that have accumulated on both sides from the founding of the Republic to the present day. The Kurdish people have no trust in the state, governments or the regime. Throughout the Republican period, almost every government has treated the Kurdish question as a security issue, a terrorism issue, and has attempted to suppress it through repression. This approach continues today. These attitudes remain deeply embedded throughout the system. title: Students in Kobanê reject incorporation of their university
content:
Students and staff at the University of Kobanê have rejected plans to incorporate their institution into the University of Aleppo. In a statement marking World Kobanê Day on November 1, they called for the university’s institutional autonomy to be preserved and for no decisions about its future to be made without the participation of its students and staff. They explicitly stated that they were not opposed to cooperation with other Syrian universities.




The statement was read out by student Gulistan Elî in front of the university building in Kobanê, in the presence of faculty members and students. It came in response to a recent decision by the Syrian Ministry of Higher Education to integrate the University of Kobanê into the state higher education system.




Opposition despite agreement with Damascus




Just on Saturday, the university administration announced the outcome of further negotiations with the Syrian government. According to the agreement, the University of Kobanê is to be incorporated into the University of Aleppo as a group of faculties while retaining its own administrative structures. Students already enrolled will be allowed to complete their studies under the existing system. Recognition of their degrees has also been guaranteed.




For the signatories of the new statement, however, these assurances are insufficient. They oppose any arrangement that coul
