author: Unknown
title: Criminal complaint filed against tree felling in Gabar and Besta
content:
In a statement issued by the bar associations’ Environment and Urban Affairs Commissions, it was reported that applications had been submitted to the chief public prosecutor’s offices in Siirt (Sêrt) and Şirnak (Şirnex) over tree felling said to have taken place between 20 April and 29 July 2025, and to have continued thereafter.




The complaint called for investigations to be opened and criminal proceedings to be brought against the relevant public officials and those carrying out the felling, over allegations of unlawful tree cutting, the transportation of illegally obtained forest products, and aiding these activities. It also requested on-site inspections of the felling and storage areas to identify and document evidence.




The bar associations called on the authorities to disclose the administrative permits authorising the felling, environmental impact assessment (EIA) decisions, information on the quantities and species of trees cut down, transport documents, and environmental inspection reports. They also urged the authorities to halt the activities.




The statement emphasised that the bar associations would continue to defend forests, wildlife, and citizens’ right to live in a healthy environment.

title: Vigil against solar power plant project in Arzoxlî enters its eighth day
content:
While legal proceedings continue against the “Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Positive” decision issued for the “Zenkar 2 Solar Power Plant and Energy Storage Facility” project, the residents of Arzoxlî, a neighbourhood of Sur in Amed, continued their vigil.




The protest began after company workers entered the project site accompanied by gendarmerie and military personnel.




The women took over the vigil on Wednesday, on the seventh day, and marched from the tent site towards the area where the company was carrying out work, chanting slogans. Soldiers once again blocked their path, while the women unfurled a banner reading: “Do not sacrifice the ancient city of Ğirap and our village to capital.”




The women continue their vigil today, the eighth day of protest.

title: DEM Party: The Republic must be updated
content:
The Turkish Republic was officially proclaimed on 29 October 1923 in Ankara, the country's new capital. In a statement titled “May the Republic endure, democracy prevail, and the brotherhood of peoples remain eternal in the second century,” the co-chairs of the DEM Party, Tülay Hatimoğulları and Tuncer Bakırhan marked the 103rd anniversary saying that citizenship could only be fully realised through an understanding that guarantees equal protection for everyone’s language, identity, culture, beliefs and opinions. The statement emphasised that Turks, Kurds and other peoples, together with all religious communities, are equal owners of the country.




The message added: “A democratic future can only be built through a shared life in which we all have an equal voice and an equal say in decision-making. A Türkiye in which women live as equals, workers enjoy security, young people have hope, and the law applies equally to everyone is possible. A Democratic Republic is one in which no one is required to be like anyone else and the will of the people is respected. This is also a vision of a country where people can live together in greater peace and harmony. An independent judiciary, the rule of law, universal human rights, a free press, the separation of powers and strong local democracy are essential to achieving this.”

title: Journalist Mavioğlu: Corruption in Turkey has become institutionalised plunder - Part One
content:
As the Peace and Democratic Society Process continues in Turkey, investigations into financial scandals, match-fixing and betting operations in football, allegations of corruption in public tenders and links to the criminal underworld have once again brought relations between politics, capital and criminal networks into focus.




Journalist Ertuğrul Mavioğlu spoke to ANF about how corruption has developed into a systematic structure over the years, the mechanisms through which public resources are transferred to capital and how this system is sustained through impunity.




Mavioğlu also discussed the current stage of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying that the state had failed to take concrete steps towards democratisation despite the measures taken by the Kurdish Freedom Movement. He argued that the struggle against corruption could not be separated from the struggle for democracy, as the weakening of oversight mechanisms and the suppression of public dissent had facilitated the plundering of public resources.




‘The state aims to dismantle the Freedom Movement’




Mavioğlu assessed the current stage of the Peace and Democratic Society Process in light of the steps taken by the Kurdish Freedom Movement and the state's response, saying that the process was still in its early stages.

title: YJA Star guerrillas: We gained our identity as resisting women through Bêrîtan
content:
Commander Bêrîtan (Gülnaz Karataş) was commemorated by her comrades in the guerrilla areas on the 34th anniversary of her martyrdom. Commander Bêrîtan was martyred in 1992 after carrying out a self-sacrificial action in Xakurkê during the war against the Turkish state and its collaborators. Bêrîtan, who became a symbol of women who refused to submit in the face of calls for surrender, established a new path of struggle. Guerrillas of the Free Women's Units (YJA Star) shared their feelings and thoughts on the anniversary of Martyr Bêrîtan's death.




YJA Star guerrilla Avaşîn Efrîn

 







 







"First of all, on the anniversary of Comrade Bêrîtan's martyrdom, we respectfully commemorate all the martyrs of freedom. We have reached this stage thanks to the efforts and truth of our pioneering martyrs. We will never forget the efforts of these heroes. Through her stance, Comrade Bêrîtan showed us the path of self-sacrifice. Bêrîtan's path is the path of freedom, and it is also the path of all martyrs. We unite around this path and educate ourselves on this basis. Particularly in this period, establishing genuine comradeship with Abdullah Öcalan is possible through a proper understanding of the martyrs. title: Shengal is at a historic turning point
content:
Shengal is now at a historic turning point. Shengal’s existence and integration bring with them a comprehensive unity with Iraq. The integration of the collective will and the genuine integration of people’s everyday lives represent the first concrete step towards bringing the two communities together in a shared life, while preserving their mother tongues and native cultures. The political reality and future represent a historic stage in which this social unity is translated into a political reality.




The coming together of the two communities through their respective cultural values and their ability to live in their mother tongues forms the cornerstone of this process. This political and cultural integration carries a force that connects with the reality of Abdullah Öcalan’s life and unites the entire society around this collective will.




This historic process expresses the will of the people of Shengal to determine their own future and live on an equal footing with Iraqi society, while also laying the foundations for building a shared future, peace and stability.




A shared political future aims to strengthen the political and social status of the Shengal region within Iraq as a whole and to permanently enshrine the people’s right to self-determination on a constitutional basis.

title: Iran sentences three protest detainees to death, whereabouts unknown
content:
Branch 23 of the Islamic Revolutionary Court in Tehran has sentenced three men arrested during the December 2025–January 2026 protests to death on charges of “espionage.”




An informed source who spoke to the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) said that the men, named Mehdi, Amir-Reza and Vahid, were notified of their sentences in Greater Tehran Central Penitentiary on 26 October.




The source added that on 28 October, the three political prisoners were summoned to the prison’s guard office on the pretext of being transferred to Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj, but were taken to an undisclosed location.




Security forces arrested the three men during the protests in Tehran and transferred them to the Greater Tehran Central Penitentiary after a period in detention. Their case was referred to Branch 23 following their indictment on charges of “espionage”, the source said.




At the time of the report, their transfer to Ghezel Hesar Prison remained unconfirmed, with no precise information available about the trial proceedings or the latest status of their cases.

title: Kurdish Peace Mothers to launch a vigil in Ankara
content:
The Peace Mothers Initiative aims to increase pressure for concrete steps in the peace and democratic society process through a multi-day vigil in the Turkish capital, Ankara. Representatives of the Peace Mothers’ Councils from 24 cities will gather on November 1, hold talks with political parties, and set up a protest tent. Their central demands include freedom for Abdullah Öcalan, action to address the situation of political prisoners, and accountability from the Turkish state for advancing the peace process.




At a press conference held at the branch of the Human Rights Association (IHD) in the province of Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır), Nezahat Teke recalled that Öcalan’s call on February 27, 2025, had raised great hopes. “However, for these hopes to develop into a genuine peace process, the state must also take action. If Öcalan is not free, any laws that are passed will be meaningless,” Teke said.




Demands for Öcalan’s freedom and improved prison conditions




The Peace Mothers are demanding that Öcalan be granted a legally and politically recognized status that would enable him to participate actively in the peace process. According to Teke, his inclusion in existing or planned commissions could make a significant contribution to advancing the process. “Our most important demand is the freedom and recognition of our leader’s status. title: Zeynep Karayılan: Peace process cannot be one-sided
content:
Discussions continue over establishing a legal framework for disarmament and the return of members of the Kurdish Freedom Movement as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, launched with the aim of achieving a democratic solution to the Kurdish question. Two years into the process, the National Security Council (MGK) has yet to issue the decision required to implement the framework law passed by parliament on 10 August with the support of 467 MPs.




The law, published in the Official Gazette on 16 August, requires security agencies to verify that disarmament has taken place, with their findings subsequently confirmed by an MGK decision before the mechanism established under the law can be activated. The absence of concrete steps towards implementation, despite parliament beginning its new legislative year and the MGK holding a meeting, has drawn criticism.




Zeynep Karayılan, Co-Chair of the Diyarbakır (Amed) Branch of the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), spoke to ANF about the legal dimensions of the process, the shortcomings of the framework law, expectations for democratisation and the steps that need to be taken.

title: Resistance against solar power project in Amed: “We will not give up our land”
content:
In the village of Arzoxlî (Turkish: Kervanpınar), in the Sur district of Amed (Diyarbakır), resistance against two planned solar power plants continues. For around a week, villagers have been maintaining a vigil in tents on the proposed project site to prevent the destruction of their communal grazing lands. Women are at the forefront of the resistance, fearing for their livelihoods and determined not to surrender the land to the energy company.




The company Zenkar plans to build two photovoltaic facilities, ZENKAR-1 and ZENKAR-2, with associated energy storage systems in Arzoxlî. The projects cover areas of approximately 22.7 and 31.3 hectares, respectively. They are designed to have a combined electricity generation capacity of 33 megawatts and an energy storage capacity of 33 megawatt-hours. The affected areas include communal grazing lands used by villagers who depend primarily on livestock farming, as well as sites of historical and cultural heritage.




Expert report raises doubts about environmental compatibility




A lawsuit challenging the positive environmental impact assessment decision for ZENKAR-2 has been filed with the Administrative Court in Amed. Following a site inspection on July 16, experts concluded that the project’s impact on agriculture, livestock farming, water resources, residential areas, and cultural heritage had not been adequately assessed. title: People’s Initiative in Qamishlo condemns attacks on returnees in Girê Spî
content:
The People’s Initiative of Qamishlo condemned attacks on people who have returned to their home region of Girê Spî (Tal Abyad). At a rally in Martyrs’ Square in Qamishlo, participants called for independent investigations into the attacks and effective protection measures for returnees.




The statement was read out by Wasil Esed, a member of the People’s Initiative, before several dozen people. The initiative demanded comprehensive, transparent, and independent investigations into all human rights violations in Raqqa and Girê Spî: "The circumstances surrounding these violations must be clarified, those responsible identified, and everyone proven to have been involved in the crimes held accountable. At the same time, immediate security measures are needed to protect people returning to their areas of origin."




Call for Kurdish-Arab solidarity




Hassan Farhan Abdulrahman al-Tay, chairman of the Council of Arab Tay Tribes, also spoke at the rally. He condemned attempts to incite tensions between Syria’s different communities. “Through our presence here, we are showing the people of Syria and the international community that we are united. We say no to division and no to those who seek to destroy relations between our peoples,” al-Tay declared.

title: Argentine Human Rights League calls for freedom for Öcalan
content:
The Argentine Human Rights League (Liga Argentina por los Derechos Humanos, LADH) has sent a letter to the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH), calling for stronger international efforts to secure the release of Abdullah Öcalan. The organization, itself a member of the federation, also proposes that the FIDH assume a guarantor role in the ongoing peace and democratic society process.




In its letter, the human rights organization, founded in 1937, pointed to the Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan’s 27 years of imprisonment on the Turkish prison island of Imrali. It said that Öcalan has spent most of this time in solitary confinement and was sentenced to aggravated life imprisonment without any ordinary prospect of release. Even the so-called right to hope—the possibility of having his detention reviewed with a realistic prospect of release—continues to be denied to the Kurdish leader, now 77-year-old, it stated.




“These demands are of crucial importance today”




In its letter, the Human Rights League acknowledges that the FIDH has already addressed Öcalan’s situation on several occasions, recognized him as a political prisoner, and called for his release. However, in light of current political developments, these efforts must be intensified, it noted.

title: Students in Dêrik demand constitutional recognition of Kurdish
content:
In the city of Dêrik in Rojava, students have once again protested against the education policies of the Syrian transitional government. They are demanding that Kurdish be officially recognized in the Syrian constitution and that the right to education in their mother tongue be guaranteed.




The demonstrators initially gathered outside the school administration building in Dêrik. They then marched to the headquarters of the regional administration, where they met with regional director Şero Şero and presented their demands.




Şero stated that he supported the students’ rights within the framework of a new, democratic Syria. He said the regional administration would forward their demands to the relevant authorities.




The protest concluded with slogans calling for the right to education in the mother tongue and the official recognition of the Kurdish language.

title: Nazan Üstündağ: Democratic integration does not mean being absorbed into the state
content:
According to sociologist Nazan Üstündağ, the democratic integration of Kurdish society must not be confused with adapting to existing state structures. Rather, she says, it involves legally recognizing Kurdish life in its entirety while strengthening society’s independent capacity for political action. Speaking to ANF, Üstündağ emphasized that the development of a democratic society must not wait for state reforms.




The academic made these remarks on the sidelines of a conference on democratic integration organized by Akademî Kurd in Zurich. The concept is one of the central topics of discussion in the ongoing peace and democratic society process. It is closely linked to Abdullah Öcalan’s concept of a democratic society and the question of how relations between the Kurdish population and the Turkish state should be shaped in the future.

title: Students in Rojava oppose the incorporation of their universities into state institutions
content:
The planned incorporation of the universities of Rojava and Kobanê into Syria’s state higher education system has met with resistance from students in Rojava. The Union of Patriotic Students rejects the recent decisions by the Syrian Ministry of Higher Education and warns that they threaten to undermine academic self-governance and Kurdish-language higher education. At a gathering at the University of Rojava in Qamishlo, the organization declared that it would not accept any decision that jeopardizes the educational structures built up over the years or the rights of students.




The dispute stems from two decisions by the Syrian Higher Education Council, announced on October 27. Under these decisions, the University of Rojava in Qamishlo is to be incorporated into the state-run Al-Furat University, while the University of Kobanê is to be placed under the University of Aleppo. Their faculties will henceforth fall under the authority of the respective state universities. Restrictions on the admission of new students are also planned for certain degree programs.




Kurdish-language education under renewed pressure

title: Kurdish athlete arrested after summons in Kermanshah, taken to undisclosed location
content:
Mohammad Nasseri, a Kurdish athlete who manages a bodybuilding gym in Harsin, Kermanshah Province, has been arrested after reporting to a prosecutor’s office in Kermanshah in response to a summons on charges of “propaganda against the state”.




The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Nasseri was arrested on 26 October after reporting to Branch 16 of the Investigating Office at Kermanshah’s Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office and was taken to an undisclosed location.




He had received the summons in recent days.

title: YJA Star guerrillas: Martyr Bêrîtan is the torch of our struggle
content:
Every year on 25 October, fighters following in the footsteps of Martyr Bêrîtan (Gülnaz Karataş) commemorate the anniversary of her action against the line of betrayal in the free mountains. The date also marks the founding of the women's army. For this reason, guerrillas, particularly women guerrillas, mark the day with great enthusiasm. Guerrillas of the Free Women's Units (YJA Star) shared their feelings on the 34th anniversary of Bêrîtan Hêvî's martyrdom.




YJA Star guerrilla Elefterya Gabar Cizîr began by commemorating Martyr Bêrîtan with respect: “Comrade Bêrîtan became a pioneer and symbol of freedom for us. She understood the reality of Abdullah Öcalan's leadership. She became an example for us and for all women. Comrade Bêrîtan recognised the reality of free women, rebelled against the mentality of betrayal and refused to surrender. Many years may have passed, but she left us a legacy of resistance. That is why we commemorate Comrade Bêrîtan every year. She became a symbol of the will and resistance of free women. Through Martyr Bêrîtan, we came to recognise the will of free women. Through her, we came to understand our own reality. Bêrîtan's personality and action shattered the sexist mentality that underestimated women's strength. This gave us tremendous morale and spiritual strength. Thanks to those martyrs, we came to understand what real life means and the path

title: KRG Interior Ministry opposes Shengal integration, calls for implementation of 9 October Agreement
content:

The Yazidi community welcomed the move, expressing satisfaction that the Iraqi state had recognised Shingal’s defence forces. They also stated that Yazidi rights should be recognised in the Iraqi Constitution in the future.

title: History repeats itself for the Turkish state
content:
The Justice and Development Party (AKP) government has recently been forming a number of alliances. While the AKP and the Nationalist Movement Party (MHP) defend these agreements, the opposition has criticised them. Various reasons have been put forward to explain these alliances. However, given that they involve the Middle East and its surrounding region, the first question that comes to mind is their connection to war. Military historians define war as the continuation of politics by other means. From this perspective, it is clear that these alliances risk drawing Turkey into the war in the Middle East.




In fact, the alliance with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan has already drawn Turkey into the war. According to incoming reports and assessments, Turkey has become involved in the ongoing war in Yemen. The Turkish state has sent its armed drones and the specialists who operate them to Saudi Arabia, from where attacks are being carried out against the Houthis in Yemen. As is known, the Houthis are supported by Iran. Turkey has therefore effectively entered into a war with Iran. On the one hand, it claims to oppose the war being waged by the United States and Israel against Iran, while on the other, it is waging war against the Houthis in Yemen.

title: Türkoğlu: We want to speak with disabled women, not for them
content:
The Women's Council and Disability Commission of the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), together with Bismil Municipality's Women's Policies Directorate and Disability and Elderly Services Unit, held a meeting with women in Bismil district of Diyarbakır (Amed) under the slogan "Disabled Women Exist Too".




The meeting was attended by DEM Party Women's Council Spokesperson Halide Türkoğlu, Disability Commission Co-Spokesperson Hatice Betül Çelebi and numerous women.







‘Ableist ideology deepens discrimination’




Halide Türkoğlu said at the meeting that disabled women faced inequality and discrimination due to both the male-dominated mentality and ableist ideology. She said that disabled women were being denied the right to make decisions about their own lives and participate in decision-making and governance processes, stressing that their problems and demands must be addressed directly with them.




Türkoğlu said: "We want to speak with disabled women, not on behalf of disabled women," and added that disabled women must be involved in decision-making processes and have control over their own lives. She said that genuine equality could only be achieved by recognising differences, bringing experiences together and leaving no woman behind.

title: The AKP cannot function without war
content:
It is becoming increasingly clear with each passing day that the process initiated by Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan through his February 27, 2025 Call for Peace and Democratic Society amounts, in a sense, to a disruption of the established game. To the domestic and international powers that divided Kurdistan into four parts, imposed genocide on the Kurds, and have benefited from the Kurdish question and the contradictions and conflicts it has generated, the message was effectively: “I will not play the game you want and impose on me. I will play my own game.” In this way, Öcalan has challenged the politics of war and moved toward adopting a politics of peace.




This new strategy and policy developed by Abdullah Öcalan has undoubtedly shocked and bewildered the forces that have tied themselves to, and benefited from, the strategy of conflict arising from the Kurdish question. It appears that the AKP is among those most taken aback. Indeed, under present conditions, when Turkey’s interests and democratic future lie in a politics of peace, the AKP remains unable to break away from its entrenched politics of war and militarization. It has failed to respond positively as required to the peace process initiated by Öcalan. title: DBP and DEM Party: We will be in Varto on 2 November
content:
The Varto (Gimgim) district organizations of the DBP and DEM Party set up a stand in Kox Square as part of the legal proceedings against the geothermal power plant project.




Speaking in a press conference, DBP District Co-Chair Aziz Oral said that the project threatens not only the natural environment but also the living spaces and cultural existence of the local population.




Oral pointed out that potential water pollution could affect agriculture and livestock farming, as well as a wider area of the Euphrates basin via the Murat River. He emphasized the need to protect nature, water resources, and the right of future generations to life.




The DBP and DEM Party called on residents to gather in the village of Xwarik on 2 November for an expert inspection related to the planned geothermal power plant (JES) project in Varto.

title: Iranian director Jafar Panahi sentenced to 5 years and 1 month in prison
content:
Iranian director and screenwriter Jafar Panahi was sentenced to 5 years and 1 month in prison in a case heard by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. The court ordered the confiscation of all his movable and immovable assets, banned him from social media activities for two years, and prohibited him from leaving the country.




According to a report by HRANA, citing Emtedad, Panahi’s lawyer, Mostafa Nili, stated that the verdict had been issued in his client’s absence. Nili said Panahi learned of the ruling after his bank accounts were frozen.




Lawyer Nili said that although his client returned to Iran on March 30, 2026, the case file listed him as being outside the country, and he had not been notified of the hearing date. Nili also stated that an arrest warrant had been issued for Panahi on May 20, 2026, and that the director currently faces three separate legal cases.




Panahi had previously been sentenced to one year in prison in a separate case on charges of “propaganda against the regime.” He was also given a two-year travel ban and prohibited from joining political and social organizations. His request for a retrial was rejected in June 2026.
